# Detection and Automation Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Make detection work end to end inside the one rtsp-warden process: a YOLOX model on ONNX Runtime (CUDA when available, CPU otherwise) fed by a working per-camera frame tap, one event per object visit with a thumbnail and an optional clip, and per-camera rules that fire named ntfy / Apprise / webhook actions, all visible in the web UI.

**Architecture:** Each camera's proxy-stream ffmpeg writes a JPEG frame tap (rate `detect_fps`, width from the largest enabled model input) into that camera's own `FrameTapDispatcher` and a single-worker `DetectorRunner`, which runs every detector at its own `fps`; `onnx` detections go through a per-camera IoU `Tracker` into an `EventBuilder` that writes one `events` row plus an atomically written thumbnail per visit, and motion goes through a `MotionBurst`. When an event opens, the camera's `RuleEngine` picks actions for a bounded drop-oldest `ActionQueue` (one `action_runs` row per run); when it closes, a `ClipScheduler` thread cuts an MP4 clip (`.ts` fallback) from the recorded segments once they are complete. Packaged migration `0003_detection_events` (applied automatically after a SQLite backup) adds the event columns and `action_runs` and drops the never-written tables, and the web layer gains event cards, an Actions page, a camera Detection panel, live preview boxes and status badges, all built on RW-0's per-camera lifecycle API.

**Tech Stack:** Python 3.11+, ONNX Runtime (`onnxruntime` CPU core dependency, `onnxruntime-gpu[cuda,cudnn]` extra), YOLOX-S / YOLOX-Nano ONNX exports (Apache-2.0), OpenCV + numpy, ffmpeg (`.ts` segments, MJPEG tap on a pipe fd), SQLAlchemy + Alembic, pydantic 2, FastAPI + Jinja2 + htmx + Alpine + Pico, httpx, Apprise, uv; tests: pytest, `onnx.helper` graphs (dev group), `httpx.MockTransport`, patched `subprocess.run` / `Popen`.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-02-detection-and-automation-design.md` (approved 2026-10-02). This plan implements sections 4 (architecture), 5 (model and inference: 5.1 runtime, 5.2 model registry, 5.3 frame tap, 5.4 legacy detectors), 6 (sampling rates), 7 (tracking and events: 7.1-7.5), 8 (rules and actions: 8.1-8.6), 9 (storage and UI: 9.1-9.4), 10 (deployment and performance), 11 (configuration summary), 12 (testing) and Appendix B. Appendix A is not in this plan: A.1 (stabilize) is merged on master, A.2 (UI pass) is the RW-2 plan.

**Branch / worktree:** `feat/detection` in WT = `/home/jcharles/Projects/python/rtsp-warden_v0.2.0/.worktrees/rw-3`. Prerequisite: RW-0 (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-02-rw0-prefork.md`) commits directly on `master` (Task 0.1 repository hygiene including the `.worktrees` ignore, Task 0.2 the per-camera lifecycle API on `AppRuntime`); this worktree is created only after both commits are on master, with `git -C /home/jcharles/Projects/python/rtsp-warden_v0.2.0 worktree add .worktrees/rw-3 -b feat/detection master`, then `uv sync --directory /home/jcharles/Projects/python/rtsp-warden_v0.2.0/.worktrees/rw-3` and a green `uv run --directory /home/jcharles/Projects/python/rtsp-warden_v0.2.0/.worktrees/rw-3 pytest -q`. ## Global Constraints

- Gate after every task: `uv run --directory <WT> pytest -q` green; `uv run --directory <WT> ruff check src/ tests/` reports no new error. The baseline is exactly 10 E501 lines: `src/rtsp_warden/app.py` (3), `src/rtsp_warden/cli.py` (2), `src/rtsp_warden/proxy/mjpeg.py:143`, `src/rtsp_warden/recorder.py:352`, `src/rtsp_warden/retention.py:138`, `tests/test_frame_tap_wiring.py:34` and `:135`. It only shrinks (Task 2 removes the two test lines, Task 11 removes `retention.py:138`); a task that touches a baseline line fixes it. `uv run --directory <WT> ruff format --check src/ tests/` clean. `mypy` is informational only.
- `uv` only (no pip, no hand-made venvs). `uv.lock` is regenerated only by `uv lock` (Task 4, needs PyPI) and committed with `pyproject.toml`; Docker builds use `uv sync --frozen`.
- Python floor: `requires-python = ">=3.11"` from Task 4 on (R2); `[tool.ruff] target-version` stays `"py310"`, so no 3.11-only syntax (`except*`).
- Secrets: never commit, print or log a credential, ntfy topic or token; configs reference `${CAM_USER}` / `${CAM_PASS}` / `${NTFY_TOKEN}`; test RTSP URLs are `rtsp://u:p@h/m`; action error text is built from status codes, never from `str(exc)`.
- `config.yaml` is authoritative and the DB never stores camera config; every write-back goes through `web/config_lock._locked_write_yaml` on the raw (unexpanded) YAML, so unknown keys and `${VAR}` text survive.
- Live segment recording stays `.ts`; MP4 appears only as a post-hoc clip remux with a `.ts` fallback (R8). Never reintroduce MP4 live segmenting.
- No Raspberry Pi or GPIO work anywhere; actions are `ntfy`, `apprise` and `webhook` only.
- `sub_url` stays optional; without it the proxy, the frame tap and clips use the main stream.
- Tests are offline: no camera, ffmpeg process, network or model weights; ONNX test graphs are built with `onnx.helper` (IR version 10, opset 17) and run on the CPU provider; ffmpeg via patched `subprocess.run` / `subprocess.Popen` looked up at call time; HTTP via `httpx.MockTransport`; time via injected `now` / `ts_unix` / `clock`; deprecation warnings via the monkeypatched module logger, never `caplog`.
- Data rules: DB datetimes are written as naive UTC and read back through `as_utc()`; numbers that reach JSON are plain `int` / `float`; thumbnails are written atomically (temp file + `os.replace`); every `DetectorRunner` that `AppRuntime` builds has `worker_count=1`.
- Commits: one per task, with the message the task gives, ending with the trailer `Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>`; never push without the owner's OK.
- Hands-off (RW-2 owns these; this track edits them only where the File ownership section names an exception): `web/templates/base.html`, `web/static/css/warden.css`, `web/static/js/warden.js`; `web/templates/cameras/list.html`, `cameras/detail.html`, `cameras/settings.html`, `cameras/form.html`, `cameras/zones.html`, `cameras/zones_editor.html`; `web/templates/partials/camera_card.html`, `partials/password_reveal.html`, `partials/flash.html`, `partials/page_header.html`, `partials/probe_result.html`; `web/templates/login.html`, `health.html`, `partials/health_status.html`, `settings/form.html`, `users/*`, `tokens/*`, `onvif/index.html`, `dashboard.html`; `web/routes/_common.py`, `auth.py`, `dashboard.py`, `settings.py`, `users.py`, `tokens.py`, `health.py`, `onvif.py`, `zones.py` (list and editor pages), `camera_edit.py`; in `web/routes/cameras.py` `cameras_list`, `camera_detail`, `camera_status`, `camera_settings`, the snapshot/live routes and their imports; `web/services/cameras.py` (`list_cameras`, `live_status`, `get_camera_by_name`), `web/services/camera_config.py`, `web/env_file.py`, `rtsp_warden/probe.py`, `rtsp_warden/ports.py`; `onvif/presets.py`, `onvif/soap.py`, `onvif/media.py`; `config.py` fields `CameraConfig.onvif_port` and `RuntimeConfig.ffprobe_path`; `cli.py` `_load_dotenv`, `_port_is_free` and the `init-config` template's camera entry and credential placeholders; `ffmpeg.redact_text`; `app._last_stderr_line`; the `docker-compose.yml` `:ro` line; the systemd unit's `ReadWritePaths` / `ReadOnlyPaths`; `packaging/systemd/install.sh`; the README and CLAUDE.md web-UI, adding-cameras and ONVIF text.
- Worktree command rules: run every command as `uv run --directory /home/jcharles/Projects/python/rtsp-warden_v0.2.0/.worktrees/rw-3 ...` (or after `cd <WT> &&` in the same command), every git command as `git -C /home/jcharles/Projects/python/rtsp-warden_v0.2.0/.worktrees/rw-3 ...`, and every file path absolute under WT; shell state does not persist between commands, and the commands work in bash and fish.

## Decisions and deviations from the spec

### Rulings this plan relies on (decisions.md)

- **R1** RW-0 lands on master first: repository hygiene plus `AppRuntime`'s per-camera lifecycle API (`_build_camera_runtime`, `_start_camera`, `_stop_camera`, `request_add/remove/restart_camera`, `_drain_requests` on the supervisor thread). Tasks 2, 11 and 12 consume it and never rewrite it.
- **R2** Python floor `>=3.11`, ruff target stays `py310`; `onnxruntime>=1.28` is a core dependency, the `gpu` extra is `onnxruntime-gpu[cuda,cudnn]>=1.28` installed with `uv sync --extra gpu --no-install-package onnxruntime --reinstall-package onnxruntime-gpu`; `onnx` is dev-only; `Dockerfile.cuda` is `python:3.13-slim` plus the pip CUDA wheels (Tasks 4, 18).
- **R4** Zones gain `kind: ignore | area` (default `ignore`, today's exclusion mask); `event.zone` is the first `area` zone containing the best box's centre; `rules[].zones` must name `area` zones; `GridMask` normalises by the decoded frame size, the saved size stays the fallback divisor (Task 8).
- **R5** The recordings pages, the timeline, `/api/recordings/{id}/timeline`, manual clip generation, the `clips` table and `detectors/categorize.py` are removed; the HLS player survives as `partials/hls_player.html`; `/htl` and `/segments` stay (Task 7).
- **R6** Migrations move into the package (`script_location = "rtsp_warden:migrations"`, Alembic `Config()` built in code); `ensure_schema()` upgrades a database behind head after copying a SQLite file to `<db>.bak-<revision>`, refuses an unknown revision, and `env.py` no longer calls `fileConfig` (Task 7).
- **R8** Clip jobs run on their own `ClipScheduler` thread, not before `ended_at + clips.post_seconds + 2 s`; input-side `-ss/-t` trims, a per-event quote-escaped concat list, a remux to `.mp4` with `-movflags +faststart`, and the concatenated `.ts` is kept when the remux fails (Tasks 11, 12).
- **R9** A config write-back that fails with `OSError` shows a message naming the path instead of a 500 (Task 15's routes).
- **R10** A camera deleted from `config.yaml` keeps its recordings, thumbnails, clips and events on disk; the events pages still resolve its media inside the configured output directories (Task 13).
- **R11** The motion detector has no debounce: a per-camera `MotionBurst` opens after `min_track_frames` consecutive motion frames and closes after `track_grace_seconds` without motion; motion rows are written only when the motion spec's `events` resolves true (explicit `true`, or unset with no enabled `onnx` spec) (Tasks 1, 9).
- **R12** Only `postprocess: yolox` ships; any other value fails validation naming the supported list; custom YOLOX-family models still drop in (Tasks 3, 5).
- **R13** The Actions-page Test calls the action class directly in a threadpool and writes no `action_runs` row; "Fire test event" inserts a real `event_type = "test"` person event with a placeholder thumbnail, runs the real `RuleEngine` with the cooldown bypassed (no stamp recorded) and the real `ActionQueue`, never queues a clip, and reports which rules matched and why others did not (Tasks 10, 12, 14, 15).
- **R14** Legacy `alerts.notifiers` is mapped onto `actions` by an `AppConfig` after-validator (enabled entries move, disabled ones stay, a name collision is an error, one warning); `alerts.enabled` is ignored; the package becomes `rtsp_warden.actions` with no shim and no `/alerts` redirect (Task 10).
- **R15** A detector's identity is its list index: the toggle is `POST /cameras/{name}/detectors/{index}/enabled`, write-back patches that one raw YAML entry through `_persist_detector_entry`, and `_persist_detectors` / `_detectors_to_list` are deleted (Task 15).
- **R16** `detect_classes` and `rules[].labels` are validated against the union of the labels of every `onnx` spec on the camera (rules may also say `motion`), skipped when the camera has no `onnx` spec; the classes page builds its groups from the model labels and gains `classes_mode = all | custom` (Tasks 3, 15).
- **R17** Actions are synchronous (`httpx.Client` per call, Apprise called directly); ntfy sends the thumbnail as the body with `title`, `message`, `filename` as query parameters and the token in `Authorization`; Apprise uses `notify(attach=path)`; webhook posts JSON; stored error text never comes from `str(exc)` (Tasks 10, 11, 14).
- **R18** The tap is always on for the proxy stream (`cam.proxy.stream`, main without `sub_url`) at `detect_fps` and the `compute_tap_settings` width (largest enabled `input_size[0]`, minimum 320); a change of the required tap settings makes `rebuild_camera_detectors` request a camera restart; each camera has its own `FrameTapDispatcher`; runners use `worker_count=1, queue_maxsize=8` (Tasks 1, 2, 12).
- **R19** Payload URLs use `runtime.public_url`, else `http://{host}:{port}` with a `0.0.0.0` / `::` bind host shown as `localhost` (Task 12).
- **R20** Thumbnails live at `<record.output_dir>/<camera>/thumbnails/<event_id>.jpg` and clips at `<record.output_dir>/<camera>/clips/<event_id>.(mp4|ts)`, stored relative to `record.output_dir`; `keep_last_n` counts only segments under `main/` and `sub/`; every camera gets a `RetentionManager`; a `clip: true` rule on a record-disabled camera warns at load and its clip is skipped (Tasks 1, 9, 11, 13).
- **R21** `record.mode: event` stays out of scope (the tap rides on the ffmpeg that event mode stops, so detection cannot start a recording); the limitation is documented only (Task 18).
- **R22** The manual Foscam check is the last task, runs only after the owner says yes, and is never a prerequisite for the gate (Task 19).

### Spec sentences replaced because the code proved their premise false

- Spec 7.4 "as the motion detector already debounces": it does not (every motion frame became an event row). Replaced by R11's `MotionBurst` (Task 9).
- Spec 8.4 "queues a clip job on the same worker": a 120 s ffmpeg run there would block notifications, and a clip cut at track close comes out silently truncated with exit code 0 (verified with ffmpeg n9.0.2). Replaced by R8's delayed `ClipScheduler` (Tasks 11, 12).
- Spec 7.3 "Zones already filter detections ... the event's `zone` is the name of the zone containing the center": every zone is an exclusion mask today, and `GridMask` divided tap-frame boxes (320 px) by the editor's saved 1920x1080 size, so every box landed in the top-left cells. Replaced by R4 (`kind: area`) and runtime frame-size normalisation (Task 8).
- Spec 5.2 "reusing the download helper in `detectors/builtin/model_utils.py`": `model_utils._download` uses `urlretrieve` with no timeout and writes straight to the final path (a truncated file looks complete). Task 3's `ensure_model_file` downloads to `.part`, verifies SHA-256, renames, and locks per path.
- Spec 5.2 `postprocess: yolox | yolo-anchor-free | ssd` and spec 12 "One test per `postprocess` type": the other two have no tensor contract. Replaced by R12 (only `yolox`, so one postprocess test family).
- Spec 5.3 / section 4 frame tap: on master the tap never reaches a detector (ffmpeg is told `pipe:3` while `pass_fds` hands over another number, one dispatcher is shared by every camera and created after the recorders, and main and sub both get a tap). Task 2 fixes this before anything builds on it.
- Spec 8.1 "implemented by the existing notifier classes moved under `actions/`": those classes are async with cached `httpx.AsyncClient`s that fail across event loops, and a non-ASCII camera name in a header raises. Rewritten synchronous per R17 (Task 10).
- Spec 9.1 drop list and backfill: `clips` is dropped too (it has an FK to `cameras`, R5), and since `EventSink` never wrote `metadata_json.camera`, `camera_name` is backfilled from the `cameras` join, then `metadata_json["camera"]`, then the EventSink message `... detected on <camera>/<stream>` (Task 7).
- Spec 9.2 "swept ... using the same age and size rules as segments": with `keep_last_n`, two thumbnails and a clip pushed every segment out of a `keep_last_n: 3` set (verified). Replaced by R20 (`keep_last_n` counts segments only) (Task 11).
- Spec 8.3 "else from the web server's bind host and port": a `0.0.0.0` bind host is not a usable link. Replaced by R19 (Task 12).
- Spec 9.3 `GET /cameras/{name}/live.mjpeg?boxes=0|1`: `camera_live` is in RW-2's part of `web/routes/cameras.py`. The annotated stream is its own route, `GET /cameras/{name}/live-boxes.mjpeg`, in RW-3's `web/routes/detection.py`; `live.mjpeg` stays the plain stream (Task 16). The same bullet's "Replaces every link to `127.0.0.1:<proxy port>`" was already done on master by the stabilize work.
- Spec 9.3 `GET /events/{id}/clip` "(serves the file, or the HLS playlist for a `.ts` clip)": the route serves the file for both kinds (`video/mp4` or `video/mp2t`) and the playlist is the sibling `GET /events/{id}/clip.m3u8` whose one entry is `/events/{id}/clip` (Task 13).
- Spec 5.1 / 10 "the camera's status panel shows a warning badge" and "Dropped-frame counts are shown on the camera status panel": the camera card and `/health` table are RW-2's files. On this branch the badge shows in the Detection panel header, the counts and warnings reach `status.json` / `rtsp-warden status` and `/health`'s Errors list, and the card include plus the `/health` "Detection" column are written out as a merge note (Task 17).

### Deviations reported by the task sections

- **Task 1:** the one-time warning helper lives in a new dependency-free `rtsp_warden/deprecations.py` (`config.py` imports `registry.py` at load, so a `DetectorSpec` validator cannot import from `config.py`); `interval_seconds` is popped by a `mode="wrap"` validator, excluded from dumps, and a converted value above `detect_fps` is clamped with a warning (only an explicit `fps` above `detect_fps` is an error); `RuleConfig.actions` is a required key and `RuleConfig` is `extra="forbid"`; `parse_between` is shared with Task 10; until Task 15 the old detectors partial shows `None` in its Interval column.
- **Task 2:** R18 is implemented as "the proxy-stream ingestor always carries the tap when it exists; the tap alone creates that ingestor only when something consumes frames", so a camera that records, proxies and detects nothing still spawns no ffmpeg; `AppRuntime.frame_tap_dispatcher` is replaced by `frame_consumers`; `_make_runner` is the single runner factory later tasks extend.
- **Task 3:** no `pyproject.toml` change (hatch already ships every non-Python file under the package; Step 16 checks a real wheel); the two SHA-256 pins come from two mirrors whose sizes match the GitHub assets and are confirmed by the first real download (Task 19); `camera_model_labels` and a `ModelError` hierarchy are added.
- **Task 4:** no `.python-version` file; `onnx>=1.17` in the dev group; a registered `gpu` pytest marker for tests that need CUDA (skipped unless the GPU build is installed).
- **Task 5:** `build_detectors_for_camera(..., *, models_dir: Path | None = None)` (optional, so existing callers keep working); `OnnxDetector.setup()` only loads a model already on disk and never raises, the first `process()` downloads, and a failure sets `error` and retries every 300 s of frame time; an unset `min_confidence` follows the camera `sensitivity`; three test files instead of one.
- **Task 6:** a tentative track that misses one update is discarded silently (spec 7.2 "consecutive"); `Track` is `eq=False`; a `ts_unix` that steps back is clamped; `active_boxes()` excludes tracks in their grace period.
- **Task 7:** `web/routes/api.py` is deleted whole (its only route was the timeline); `alembic.ini` stays at the repo root for the Alembic CLI only; three unavoidable edits in RW-2 files (`camera_detail` in `web/routes/cameras.py`, `web/routes/dashboard.py`) that resolve at the rebase by taking RW-2's version minus the `list_recordings` lines; `cameras/detail.html`'s "Recent recordings" block is left for RW-2 to delete.
- **Task 8:** the editor's kind control is a new RW-3 partial `partials/zone_kind.html` added to RW-2's `cameras/zones_editor.html` with one include line; `save_zone` / `delete_zone` answer 422 for an unknown kind, a bad zone name, or a change a rule would reject; disabled `area` zones are valid rule targets that never match.
- **Task 9:** `detectors/runner.py` and `detectors/sinks.py` are replaced whole (re-implementing Task 2's guard and Task 8's frame-size filtering); `EventSink(db=None)`; runner status rows add `setup_error`; a runner with tracker / builder / burst and `worker_count > 1` is a `ValueError`; nothing is wired into `app.py` until Task 12.
- **Task 10:** `NtfyActionSpec` gains `priority` (1..5, carried from legacy entries) and an optional `topic`; action names are stripped, at most 64 characters and free of `/`, webhook headers ASCII; duplicate names are an error in every combination (actions, legacy enabled or not); the one deprecation warning also names entries left in `alerts.notifiers`; `AppConfig.model_config` hides input in errors; `RuleDecision` fields default empty, `Action` is `runtime_checkable`, `RuleEngine` adds `rules` and `reset_cooldowns()`, a cooldown stamp in the future does not suppress; `Action.test()` sends a synthetic payload with a placeholder JPEG through the real `send`; the Alerts routes are deleted here and the Actions page is Task 14 (the nav link is dead between Tasks 10 and 14).
- **Task 11:** two ffmpeg runs (concat + trim to `<id>.ts`, then remux to `<id>.mp4`), so an MP4 keeps up to one GOP of pre-roll; `max_duration` caps the window from its start; a segment ends where the next starts, capped at `chunk_seconds + 10 s`; the concat list holds absolute paths and is deleted in `finally`; clips keep `-an`; a failed clip is only logged; `ClipsConfig.output_dir` becomes unused but stays in the model so existing configs load (Task 18 documents where old MP4s were).
- **Task 12:** `Tracker`, `EventBuilder` and `MotionBurst` are built in `_make_runner` (fresh on every rebuild) while the `RuleEngine` lives on `CameraRuntime.rule_engine` (cooldowns survive a hot reload); `AppRuntime.detection_status(name)` and `find_runner(name)` replace the skeleton's `CameraRuntime.detector_status()`; provider printing in `rtsp-warden status` moves to Task 17; added `RuntimeConfig.public_url`, `dispatch_event`, `tap_settings_for`, `cli._public_url`, `cli._onnx_providers`, `cli._onnx_device_check`; restart-on-tap-change also covers the first detector on a camera without an ingest and asks for at most one pending restart per camera.
- **Task 13:** `web/routes/dashboard.py` (RW-2's) is not edited; "Detections today" is fixed in the service and passing `cfg=cfg` from the dashboard is a one-line follow-up after the RW-2 merge; new htmx fragment `events/_grid.html`; query parameters become `camera`, `label`, `from`, `to` (local days, `to` inclusive) and a 1-based `page` of 24 cards; the service queries `Event` directly (label fallback for pre-0003 rows, local-time windows).
- **Task 14:** the page also lists the camera rules that name each action (`used_by`); no CSS changes (Pico's `<ins>` / `<mark>`); the Test handler is a plain `def` so FastAPI runs it in the threadpool.

- **Task 16:** the runner is looked up per frame (a rebuild replaces it); boxes older than `max(1.5 s, 2 / slowest enabled non-motion fps)` are not drawn; the switch's storage access lives in Alpine `init()` / `save()` methods.
- **Task 17:** the RW-2 templates (`camera_card.html`, `health_status.html`) and `web/routes/health.py` are not edited on this branch (merge note with tests instead); the pure summary is `status_model.camera_detection_summary` (not `camera_detection_status`, to avoid a name clash with Task 15); no Prometheus gauge.
- **Task 18:** the Foscam example's RTSP port is 554 (the owner's port forward) instead of the old 5554, **for the owner to confirm**; `Dockerfile` and `Dockerfile.distroless` stay unchanged; README config blocks carry `<!-- config-example: ... -->` markers that the tests validate.
- **Task 19:** never a gate; records five known risks ahead of time: K1 httpx logs the ntfy URL (topic) at INFO (fix site `logging_utils.py`, in neither ownership list), K2 a detector toggle during a stalled download can block on the detector lock for up to the 60 s timeout, K3 a brisk walk at `fps: 2` may split into several events, K4 a rule may not fire when the event opens below its `min_confidence`, K5 `/status.json`'s ffmpeg `stderr_tail` may contain the expanded camera URL.

## Review Focus

1. **An existing 0002 SQLite database:** the first `serve` after the upgrade migrates it to `0003_detection_events` exactly once, leaves one `<db>.bak-0002_clips` copy, and a second start neither backfills again nor makes a second backup; pinned by Task 7 (`TestEnsureSchemaAlembic::test_ensure_schema_upgrades_a_0002_database_once_and_backs_it_up`, Step 12).
2. **Two overlapping people, or one person standing still:** two people whose boxes overlap (IoU about 0.33) become two events, and a person seen every second for ten minutes becomes one event, not several; pinned by Task 6 (`test_two_overlapping_people_stay_two_tracks`, `test_person_standing_still_for_ten_minutes_is_one_track`, Step 6) and end to end through runner and EventBuilder by Task 9 (`test_two_overlapping_people_become_two_events`, `test_person_standing_still_for_ten_minutes_is_one_event`, Step 9).
3. **An offline home lab whose `onnx` model file is absent and cannot be downloaded:** the camera keeps recording, `serve` start and a hot reload neither wait on nor crash from the download, and the error shows on the Detection panel and in the status surfaces; pinned by Task 12 (`test_a_model_that_cannot_load_keeps_recording_and_hot_reload_alive`, Step 13), with its parts pinned by Task 3 (Step 6), Task 5 (Step 7), Task 15 (Step 6) and Task 17 (Step 10).
4. **An existing config with `interval_seconds: 1.0`:** it loads, the detector runs at 1 fps on a 5 fps tap, and the deprecation warning is logged exactly once per process (write-back round trips never re-trigger it); pinned by Task 1 (`test_existing_interval_config_loads_and_warns_once_per_process`, Step 10) and Task 9 (`test_interval_seconds_one_runs_the_detector_at_one_fps`, Step 9).
5. **An overnight `between` window across DST:** a rule with `between: "22:00-06:00"` matches at 23:30 and at 05:30 local time, not at 12:00, and every minute of both DST change days evaluates without raising; pinned by Task 10 (`test_between_night_window_in_a_real_zone`, `test_between_across_dst_transitions_never_raises`, Step 6).

### Task 1: Config: camera and detector fields, tap settings, deprecations (part 1)

Goal: every new configuration key that the detection pipeline reads exists, validates and round-trips, and the
frame tap's rate and width come from the camera config instead of hard-coded `StreamIngestor` defaults. Nothing
reads the new keys at runtime yet except the tap plumbing (`detect_fps` reaches ffmpeg's `-r`). Later tasks
consume them: Task 3 (label validation), Task 8 (`rules[].zones`), Task 9 (per-detector `fps`, motion `events`),
Task 10 (`rules[].actions`, `between`), Task 12 (tap width from the model registry).

Facts this task is built on (verified on master `e5623cb`; RW-0 does not touch any file this task edits):
- `config.py:12` imports `DetectorSpec` from `detectors/registry.py` at module load, and `registry.py` imports
  `CameraConfig` only under `TYPE_CHECKING` (`registry.py:187-191`). A validator on `DetectorSpec` therefore
  cannot import anything from `config.py` at module top (config map G9). The one-time warning helper lives in a
  new dependency-free module, `rtsp_warden/deprecations.py`, which both files import.
- `DetectorSpec.interval_seconds: float = 1.0` (`registry.py:38`) is never read by the runtime (ingest map H8).
  Spec section 6: keep accepting it for one release, convert `fps = 1 / interval_seconds`, warn once naming
  `fps`. If it stayed a defaulted field, every `model_dump` round trip would re-add `interval_seconds: 1.0` and
  silently set `fps = 1.0` on the next load (config map G8). It becomes `float | None`, is popped by the
  validator (so it is always `None` after validation) and is excluded from dumps.
- A converted `interval_seconds` can exceed `detect_fps` (for example `interval_seconds: 0.1` -> 10 fps). Such
  configs load today, so the converted value is clamped to `detect_fps` with a one-time warning; only an explicit
  `fps` above `detect_fps` is a validation error (spec 6). The clamp needs to know where `fps` came from, so
  `_convert_interval` is a `mode="wrap"` model validator that sets a private attribute after core validation.
- `frame_tap_fps` is typed `int` and rendered `str(int(frame_tap_fps))` (`ffmpeg.py:400, 546`;
  `recorder.py:57`), so `detect_fps: 0.5` would become `-r 0` (ingest map G11). ffmpeg accepts `-r 0.5` for the
  MJPEG tap output. `CameraRecorder._build_ingestor` (`recorder.py:407-420`) never passes tap fps or width.
- Deprecation warnings are tested by monkeypatching the module logger (`deprecations.log.warning`), never
  `caplog`: `migrations/env.py` runs `fileConfig` during `ensure_schema()` and disables existing loggers.
- No config model sets `validate_assignment`; routes mutate specs in memory. `CameraConfig.effective_fps`
  therefore clamps to `detect_fps` even when `spec.fps` was edited after validation.
- `load_config` raises `SystemExit("Config validation failed: ...")`, not `ValidationError`
  (`config.py:565-572`). Model tests call `model_validate` and expect `pydantic.ValidationError`.

  ```python
  # src/rtsp_warden/deprecations.py (new; imports nothing from the package)
  log: logging.Logger                      # "rtsp_warden.deprecations"; tests monkeypatch log.warning
  _WARNED: set[str]                        # keys already warned; tests monkeypatch it to a fresh set()
  def warn_once(key: str, msg: str, *args: object) -> None   # logs msg % args once per key per process

  # src/rtsp_warden/detectors/registry.py
  DetectorType = Literal["motion", "person", "vehicle", "dnn", "custom", "onnx"]
  DetectorDevice = Literal["auto", "cuda", "cpu"]
  LEGACY_DETECTOR_TYPES: frozenset[str]    # {"person", "vehicle", "dnn"}
  class DetectorSpec(BaseModel):           # existing fields unchanged, plus:
      interval_seconds: float | None = Field(default=None, exclude=True)  # deprecated; always None after validation
      fps: float | None = None             # > 0; None = the camera's detect_fps
      model: str | None = None             # onnx registry name; None means "yolox-s" (resolved by Task 5)
      device: DetectorDevice = "auto"
      events: bool | None = None           # motion only; None = CameraConfig.motion_events_enabled decides
      _fps_from_interval: bool = PrivateAttr(default=False)   # True when fps came from interval_seconds
      # @model_validator(mode="wrap") _convert_interval: interval_seconds -> fps = 1/v when fps is None,
      #   explicit fps wins; warn_once key f"interval_seconds:{type}:{v:g}"; v <= 0 or non-number -> error
      # @field_validator("type") _warn_legacy: person/vehicle/dnn -> warn_once key f"detector-type:{v}"
      # @field_validator("fps") _fps_positive: "fps must be > 0"

  # src/rtsp_warden/config.py
  from .deprecations import warn_once as _warn_once   # config._warn_once(key, msg, *args) -> None
  DETECT_FPS_MIN = 0.5
  DETECT_FPS_MAX = 30.0
  TAP_MIN_WIDTH = 320
  def parse_between(spec: str) -> tuple[datetime.time, datetime.time]   # "HH:MM-HH:MM", may wrap midnight
  class RuleConfig(BaseModel):             # model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", hide_input_in_errors=True)
      name: str                            # stripped, 1-64 chars
      labels: list[str] = []               # empty = any label
      zones: list[str] = []                # empty = any zone (names checked against area zones in Task 8)
      min_confidence: float = 0.0          # 0..1
      between: str | None = None           # normalised "HH:MM-HH:MM"; "" -> None
      cooldown_seconds: float = 60.0       # >= 0
      clip: bool = False
      actions: list[str]                   # required key (may be []); names checked in Task 10
  class CameraConfig(BaseModel):           # existing fields unchanged, plus:
      detect_fps: float = 5.0              # DETECT_FPS_MIN..DETECT_FPS_MAX
      track_grace_seconds: float = 3.0     # > 0
      min_track_frames: int = 2            # >= 1
      rules: list[RuleConfig] = []         # names unique per camera
      # @model_validator(mode="after") _detector_rates: explicit spec.fps > detect_fps -> ValueError
      #   "detectors[i] (type): fps X is above the camera's detect_fps Y ..."; fps from interval_seconds -> clamped
      # @model_validator(mode="after") _rules_valid: duplicate rule name -> ValueError; clip rule with
      #   record.enabled false -> one-time warning (R20)
      def effective_fps(self, spec: DetectorSpec) -> float          # spec.fps or detect_fps, never above detect_fps
      def motion_events_enabled(self, spec: DetectorSpec) -> bool   # spec.events if set, else no enabled onnx spec
  def compute_tap_settings(
      cam: CameraConfig,
      input_width_for: Callable[[DetectorSpec], int | None] = _no_input_width,   # default returns None
  ) -> tuple[float, int]                   # (float(detect_fps), max(TAP_MIN_WIDTH, widths of enabled specs))

  # src/rtsp_warden/recorder.py
  StreamIngestor.frame_tap_fps: float = 5.0
  CameraRecorder.tap_settings: tuple[float, int] | None = None   # None -> compute_tap_settings(camera)

  # src/rtsp_warden/ffmpeg.py
  build_ffmpeg_ingest_cmd(..., frame_tap_fps: float = 5.0, ...)   # tap output "-r" is f"{frame_tap_fps:g}"
  ```

```python
"""Config for detection and automation (RW-3 Task 1).

Covers the one-time deprecation helper, the new DetectorSpec fields and
deprecations, the camera-level detection fields, rules, and the frame tap
settings the recorder hands to ffmpeg.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import pytest

from rtsp_warden import deprecations


@pytest.fixture
def warnings_seen(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> list[str]:
    """Capture deprecation warnings, starting from an empty once-only registry.

    The module logger is patched directly (not caplog): Alembic's fileConfig
    disables existing loggers once any DB test has run.
    """
    messages: list[str] = []
    monkeypatch.setattr(deprecations, "_WARNED", set())
    monkeypatch.setattr(deprecations.log, "warning", lambda msg, *args: messages.append(msg % args))
    return messages


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# deprecations.warn_once
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_warn_once_logs_first_call_only(warnings_seen: list[str]) -> None:
    deprecations.warn_once("k1", "old %s is deprecated", "thing")
    deprecations.warn_once("k1", "old %s is deprecated", "thing")
    deprecations.warn_once("k2", "other %s", "key")
    assert warnings_seen == ["old thing is deprecated", "other key"]
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Implement `rtsp_warden/deprecations.py`**

Create `/home/jcharles/Projects/python/rtsp-warden_v0.2.0/.worktrees/rw-3/src/rtsp_warden/deprecations.py` with exactly:

```python
"""One-time deprecation warnings for config keys and detector types.

Config models are validated more than once per process (startup, web
write-back round trips, hot reload), so every deprecation goes through
``warn_once``: the first call with a given key logs, later calls are silent.
This module imports nothing from the package, so both ``config.py`` and
``detectors/registry.py`` can use it without an import cycle.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import threading

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

_WARNED: set[str] = set()
_LOCK = threading.Lock()


def warn_once(key: str, msg: str, *args: object) -> None:
    """Log ``msg % args`` as a warning the first time ``key`` is seen in this process."""
    with _LOCK:
        if key in _WARNED:
            return
        _WARNED.add(key)
    log.warning(msg, *args)
```

`warn_once` reads the module globals `_WARNED` and `log` at call time, which is what lets the test fixture swap
them with `monkeypatch`.

with:

```python
    # ROI and privacy masks (Batch 4)
    roi: list[tuple[int, int]] | None = None
    masks: list[list[tuple[int, int]]] | None = None

    # True when `fps` was derived from a deprecated `interval_seconds`. Lets
    # CameraConfig clamp such a value to detect_fps instead of rejecting it.
    _fps_from_interval: bool = PrivateAttr(default=False)

    @model_validator(mode="wrap")
    @classmethod
    def _convert_interval(
        cls, data: Any, handler: ModelWrapValidatorHandler[DetectorSpec]
    ) -> DetectorSpec:
        """Accept the deprecated `interval_seconds` key and convert it to `fps`.

        `fps = 1 / interval_seconds` when `fps` is not set; an explicit `fps`
        wins. Either way the key is dropped and a one-time warning is logged.
        """
        converted = False
        if isinstance(data, dict) and data.get("interval_seconds") is not None:
            data = dict(data)
            raw = data.pop("interval_seconds")
            try:
                interval = float(raw)
            except (TypeError, ValueError):
                raise ValueError("interval_seconds must be a number") from None
            if not interval > 0:
                raise ValueError("interval_seconds must be > 0")
            det_type = data.get("type")
            key = f"interval_seconds:{det_type}:{interval:g}"
            if data.get("fps") is None:
                data["fps"] = 1.0 / interval
                converted = True
                warn_once(
                    key,
                    "detectors[].interval_seconds is deprecated and will be removed in the "
                    "next release; use fps (type=%s: interval_seconds %g became fps %g)",
                    det_type,
                    interval,
                    data["fps"],
                )
            else:
                warn_once(
                    key,
                    "detectors[].interval_seconds is deprecated and is ignored because fps "
                    "is also set (type=%s); remove interval_seconds",
                    det_type,
                )
        spec = handler(data)
        if converted:
            spec._fps_from_interval = True
        return spec

    @field_validator("type")
    @classmethod
    def _warn_legacy(cls, v: str) -> str:
        if v in LEGACY_DETECTOR_TYPES:
            warn_once(
                f"detector-type:{v}",
                "detector type %r is deprecated and will be removed in the next release; "
                "use type: onnx (model: yolox-s)",
                v,
            )
        return v

    @field_validator("fps")
    @classmethod
    def _fps_positive(cls, v: float | None) -> float | None:
        if v is not None and not v > 0:
            raise ValueError("fps must be > 0")
        return v
```

with:

```python
    @field_validator("sensitivity")
    @classmethod
    def _sensitivity_range(cls, v: float) -> float:
        if not 0.0 <= v <= 100.0:
            raise ValueError("sensitivity must be between 0.0 and 100.0")
        return v

    @field_validator("detect_fps")
    @classmethod
    def _detect_fps_range(cls, v: float) -> float:
        if not DETECT_FPS_MIN <= v <= DETECT_FPS_MAX:
            raise ValueError(
                f"detect_fps must be between {DETECT_FPS_MIN:g} and {DETECT_FPS_MAX:g}"
            )
        return v

    @field_validator("track_grace_seconds")
    @classmethod
    def _grace_positive(cls, v: float) -> float:
        if not v > 0:
            raise ValueError("track_grace_seconds must be > 0")
        return v

    @field_validator("min_track_frames")
    @classmethod
    def _min_frames_positive(cls, v: int) -> int:
        if v < 1:
            raise ValueError("min_track_frames must be >= 1")
        return v

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _fallback_proxy_stream(self) -> CameraConfig:
        """Without a sub stream, the proxy (and frame tap) read the main stream."""
        if self.sub_url is None and self.proxy.stream == "sub":
            self.proxy.stream = "main"
        return self

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _detector_rates(self) -> CameraConfig:
        """A detector cannot run faster than the tap: every spec fps <= detect_fps.

        An fps that came from the deprecated interval_seconds is clamped with a
        warning instead, so a config that loaded before keeps loading.
        """
        for i, spec in enumerate(self.detectors):
            if spec.fps is None or spec.fps <= self.detect_fps:
                continue
            if spec._fps_from_interval:
                _warn_once(
                    f"interval-clamp:{self.name}:{i}",
                    "camera %r detectors[%d] (%s): interval_seconds gives fps %g, above "
                    "detect_fps %g; using fps %g",
                    self.name,
                    i,
                    spec.type,
                    spec.fps,
                    self.detect_fps,
                    self.detect_fps,
                )
                spec.fps = self.detect_fps
                continue
            raise ValueError(
                f"detectors[{i}] ({spec.type}): fps {spec.fps:g} is above the camera's "
                f"detect_fps {self.detect_fps:g}; lower fps or raise detect_fps"
            )
        return self

    def effective_fps(self, spec: DetectorSpec) -> float:
        """The rate a detector runs at: its own fps, else detect_fps, never above detect_fps."""
        if spec.fps is None:
            return float(self.detect_fps)
        return float(min(spec.fps, self.detect_fps))

    def motion_events_enabled(self, spec: DetectorSpec) -> bool:
        """Whether a motion spec writes events rows (spec 7.4, 11).

        An explicit `events` wins. Unset means yes, unless the camera has an
        enabled `onnx` detector.
        """
        if spec.events is not None:
            return spec.events
        return not any(s.type == "onnx" and s.enabled for s in self.detectors)
```

```python
name: yard
main_url: rtsp://u:p@h/m
detect_fps: 5
detectors:

rules:
```

```python
DETECT_FPS_MIN = 0.5
```

```python
_BETWEEN_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*(\d{1,2}):(\d{2})\s*-\s*(\d{1,2}):(\d{2})\s*$")


def parse_between(spec: str) -> tuple[time, time]:
    """Parse a rule window "HH:MM-HH:MM" (local time) into (start, end).

    The window may wrap midnight ("22:00-06:00"). Raises ValueError for a
    malformed value, an hour above 23, a minute above 59, or start == end.
    """
    m = _BETWEEN_RE.match(spec)
    if m is None:
        raise ValueError(f"between must look like 'HH:MM-HH:MM', got {spec!r}")
    h1, m1, h2, m2 = (int(g) for g in m.groups())
    if h1 > 23 or h2 > 23 or m1 > 59 or m2 > 59:
        raise ValueError(f"between needs hours 00-23 and minutes 00-59, got {spec!r}")
    start, end = time(h1, m1), time(h2, m2)
    if start == end:
        raise ValueError(f"between start and end are the same time: {spec!r}")
    return start, end


class RuleConfig(BaseModel):
    """A per-camera rule: which events fire which actions (spec 8.2).

    An event matches when its label is in `labels` (empty = any), its zone is in
    `zones` (empty = any), its confidence is >= `min_confidence`, and the local
    time is inside `between` when set. `actions` names entries of the top-level
    `actions` list. Unknown keys are an error so a typo such as `lables:` cannot
    silently turn a rule into "match everything".
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", hide_input_in_errors=True)

    name: str
    labels: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    zones: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    min_confidence: float = 0.0
    between: str | None = None  # "HH:MM-HH:MM" local time, may wrap midnight
    cooldown_seconds: float = 60.0
    clip: bool = False
    actions: list[str]

    @field_validator("name")
    @classmethod
    def _name_valid(cls, v: str) -> str:
        v2 = v.strip()
        if not v2:
            raise ValueError("rule name must be non-empty")
        if len(v2) > 64:
            raise ValueError("rule name must be at most 64 characters")
        return v2

    @field_validator("labels", "zones", "actions")
    @classmethod
    def _names_nonempty(cls, v: list[str]) -> list[str]:
        out = [item.strip() for item in v]
        if any(not item for item in out):
            raise ValueError("list entries must be non-empty names")
        return out

    @field_validator("min_confidence")
    @classmethod
    def _confidence_range(cls, v: float) -> float:
        if not 0.0 <= v <= 1.0:
            raise ValueError("min_confidence must be between 0.0 and 1.0")
        return v

    @field_validator("between", mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def _between_format(cls, v: Any) -> Any:
        if v is None:
            return None
        if not isinstance(v, str):
            raise ValueError("between must be a quoted string like '22:00-06:00'")
        if not v.strip():
            return None
        start, end = parse_between(v)
        return f"{start:%H:%M}-{end:%H:%M}"

    @field_validator("cooldown_seconds")
    @classmethod
    def _cooldown_non_negative(cls, v: float) -> float:
        if not v >= 0:
            raise ValueError("cooldown_seconds must be >= 0")
        return v


class CameraConfig(BaseModel):
```

```python
def _no_input_width(spec: DetectorSpec) -> int | None:
    return None


def compute_tap_settings(
    cam: CameraConfig,
    input_width_for: Callable[[DetectorSpec], int | None] = _no_input_width,
) -> tuple[float, int]:
    """Return the frame tap's (fps, scale width) for a camera (spec 5.3).

    fps is the camera's detect_fps. The width is the largest model input width
    among the camera's enabled detectors, as reported by `input_width_for`
    (None for a detector without a model input), and never below TAP_MIN_WIDTH.
    """
    width = TAP_MIN_WIDTH
    for spec in cam.detectors:
        if not spec.enabled:
            continue
        w = input_width_for(spec)
        if w is not None and w > width:
            width = int(w)
    return float(cam.detect_fps), width


# --- Sprint 4: event recording + alerts + ONVIF config types ---
```

### Task 2: The frame tap works: per-camera dispatcher, correct pipe fd, proxy stream only, ordered runner

**Why.** Today no detector ever sees a frame, and turning the tap on would kill recording:
- **H1** `AppRuntime.build()` builds every `CameraRecorder` with `frame_tap_dispatcher=self.frame_tap_dispatcher`
  (None in a default `serve`) and only afterwards `_build_detectors()` creates a dispatcher, so no ingestor gets a tap.
- **H2** `StreamIngestor.start()` (recorder.py:133) tells ffmpeg `pipe:3`, but `Popen(pass_fds=(w_fd,))` hands the
  write end to the child under its *own* number (5, 7, ...). ffmpeg fails to open `pipe:3` (rc 247) and the segment
  output dies with it. The parent also keeps its write end until `stop()`, so the reader never sees EOF, and
  `stop()` never closes the read end (one fd leaked per supervisor restart).
- **H3** one shared dispatcher feeds every camera's frames to every runner, and both main and sub get a tap.
- Runners use `worker_count=2` on one queue of 32: two frames of one camera run through the same stateful detector
  concurrently, and drop-oldest keeps frames ~6 s stale.

This task fixes all four. After it, every camera has its own `FrameTapDispatcher` on `CameraRuntime.dispatcher`,
created **before** its recorder; only the ingestor of `cam.proxy.stream` carries the tap (main when there is no
`sub_url`); ffmpeg is told `pipe:<w_fd>`; the parent closes its write end right after the spawn and the reader
thread owns and closes the read end; runners built by `AppRuntime` use one worker, a queue of 8 and `camera=<name>`.
`--frame-consumer` consumers are appended to every camera's dispatcher. Ruling R18 ("tap always on for the proxy
stream") is implemented as: the proxy-stream ingestor always carries the tap when it exists; the tap alone creates
that ingestor only when something consumes it (enabled detectors without `--no-detectors`, or a `--frame-consumer`),
so a camera that records nothing, proxies nothing and detects nothing still spawns no ffmpeg.

- [ ] **Step 2: Write the failing fd tests**

Create `/home/jcharles/Projects/python/rtsp-warden_v0.2.0/.worktrees/rw-3/tests/test_recorder_tap_fd.py` with exactly
this content. `subprocess.Popen` is faked at call time (nothing is spawned). The fake behaves like the real ffmpeg
child: `Popen` gives a child only fds 0-2 and `pass_fds`, under their parent numbers, so the fake writes two JPEG
frames to the fd its last argument names only when that fd is in `pass_fds`. `os.pipe` and `os.close` are wrapped to
record what was opened and closed.

```python
"""The frame tap pipe: ffmpeg is told the fd it really gets, and no tap fd leaks.

``subprocess.Popen`` is replaced by ``_FakeChild``, which behaves like the ffmpeg child.
Popen hands a child only fds 0-2 and ``pass_fds``, under their parent numbers, so the fake
writes two JPEG frames to the fd named by its last argument (the tap is always the last
ffmpeg output) only when that fd is in ``pass_fds``, and otherwise fails the way ffmpeg
does (rc 247, "Bad file descriptor"). Nothing real is spawned.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import subprocess
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import pytest

from rtsp_warden.config import RuntimeConfig, StreamRecordConfig
from rtsp_warden.frame_tap import FrameTapDispatcher
from rtsp_warden.recorder import StreamIngestor

FRAME_ONE = b"\xff\xd8one\xff\xd9"
FRAME_TWO = b"\xff\xd8two\xff\xd9"


class _Collect:
    """FrameConsumer that keeps every frame it is given."""

    name = "collect"

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.frames: list[tuple[str, str, bytes]] = []

    def on_frame(self, camera: str, stream: str, jpeg_bytes: bytes, ts_unix: float) -> None:
        self.frames.append((camera, stream, jpeg_bytes))


class _FakeChild:
    """subprocess.Popen stand-in for an ffmpeg that writes two tap frames, then exits."""

    def __init__(self, args: list[str], *, pass_fds: tuple[int, ...] = (), **_kw: Any) -> None:
        self.args = list(args)
        self.pass_fds = tuple(pass_fds)
        self.stdout = None
        self.stderr = None
        self.pid = 4242
        self.returncode = 0
        target = self.args[-1]
        if target.startswith("pipe:"):
            fd = int(target.split(":", 1)[1])
            if fd in self.pass_fds:
                os.write(fd, FRAME_ONE + FRAME_TWO)
            else:
                self.returncode = 247  # the fd is not open in the child

    def poll(self) -> int:
        return self.returncode


@dataclass
class _Spy:
    pipes: list[tuple[int, int]] = field(default_factory=list)
    closed: list[int] = field(default_factory=list)
    children: list[_FakeChild] = field(default_factory=list)


@pytest.fixture
def spy(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> _Spy:
    """Record every os.pipe() pair, every os.close() and every (fake) child spawned."""
    seen = _Spy()
    real_pipe, real_close = os.pipe, os.close

    def pipe() -> tuple[int, int]:
        pair = real_pipe()
        seen.pipes.append(pair)
        return pair

    def close(fd: int) -> None:
        seen.closed.append(fd)
        real_close(fd)

    def popen(args: list[str], **kw: Any) -> _FakeChild:
        child = _FakeChild(args, **kw)
        seen.children.append(child)
        return child

    monkeypatch.setattr(os, "pipe", pipe)
    monkeypatch.setattr(os, "close", close)
    monkeypatch.setattr(subprocess, "Popen", popen)
    return seen


def _tap_only(sink: _Collect) -> StreamIngestor:
    """An ingestor whose only ffmpeg output is the frame tap."""
    return StreamIngestor(
        camera_name="cam",
        stream_name="main",
        upstream_url="rtsp://u:p@h/m",
        runtime=RuntimeConfig(),
        record_cfg=StreamRecordConfig(enabled=False, container="ts"),
        frame_tap_enabled=True,
        frame_tap_dispatcher=FrameTapDispatcher(consumers=(sink,)),
    )


def _join_reader(ing: StreamIngestor) -> None:
    reader = ing._frame_tap_thread
    assert reader is not None
    reader.join(timeout=2.0)
    assert not reader.is_alive()


def test_tap_argv_names_the_fd_the_child_receives(spy: _Spy) -> None:
    sink = _Collect()
    ing = _tap_only(sink)

    ing.start()
    try:
        child = spy.children[0]
        assert child.args[-1] == f"pipe:{child.pass_fds[0]}"
        assert child.returncode == 0
        _join_reader(ing)
        assert sink.frames == [("cam", "main", FRAME_ONE), ("cam", "main", FRAME_TWO)]
    finally:
        ing.stop()


def test_parent_drops_the_write_end_and_the_reader_closes_the_read_end(spy: _Spy) -> None:
    ing = _tap_only(_Collect())

    ing.start()
    try:
        r_fd, w_fd = spy.pipes[0]
        assert ing.frame_tap_write_fd is None
        assert w_fd in spy.closed
        # EOF reaches the reader only once no write end is open anywhere, so the reader
        # exiting proves the parent let go of its copy as soon as ffmpeg was spawned.
        _join_reader(ing)
        assert r_fd in spy.closed
    finally:
        ing.stop()

    # Nothing is closed twice: a freed fd number may already belong to another camera.
    assert spy.closed.count(w_fd) == 1
    assert spy.closed.count(r_fd) == 1


def test_restarts_do_not_leak_tap_fds(spy: _Spy) -> None:
    ing = _tap_only(_Collect())

    for _ in range(3):  # what the supervisor does after every ffmpeg crash
        ing.start()
        _join_reader(ing)
        ing.stop()

    assert len(spy.pipes) == 3
    # fd numbers are reused from one cycle to the next, so count per number: every
    # opening of a tap fd is matched by exactly one close.
    opened = [fd for pair in spy.pipes for fd in pair]
    for fd in set(opened):
        assert spy.closed.count(fd) == opened.count(fd)


def test_a_failed_spawn_closes_both_tap_fds(spy: _Spy, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    def no_ffmpeg(args: list[str], **_kw: Any) -> _FakeChild:
        raise FileNotFoundError(2, "No such file or directory", "ffmpeg")

    monkeypatch.setattr(subprocess, "Popen", no_ffmpeg)
    ing = _tap_only(_Collect())

    with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
        ing.start()

    r_fd, w_fd = spy.pipes[0]
    assert r_fd in spy.closed
    assert w_fd in spy.closed
    assert ing.frame_tap_write_fd is None
    assert ing._frame_tap_read_fd is None
    assert ing._frame_tap_thread is None
    ing.stop()
    assert spy.closed.count(r_fd) == 1
    assert spy.closed.count(w_fd) == 1


def test_a_tap_without_a_dispatcher_opens_no_pipe(spy: _Spy, tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    ing = StreamIngestor(
        camera_name="cam",
        stream_name="main",
        upstream_url="rtsp://u:p@h/m",
        runtime=RuntimeConfig(),
```

```python
    def _close_frame_tap_write_fd(self) -> None:
        """Close the parent's tap write end once; the field is cleared before the close."""
        fd, self._frame_tap_write_fd = self._frame_tap_write_fd, None
        if fd is not None:
            try:
                os.close(fd)
            except OSError:
                pass

    def _close_frame_tap_read_fd(self) -> None:
        """Close a tap read end no reader thread took over; the field is cleared first."""
        fd, self._frame_tap_read_fd = self._frame_tap_read_fd, None
        if fd is not None:
            try:
                os.close(fd)
            except OSError:
                pass
```

Clearing the field before `os.close` matters: a freed fd number is reused at once by the next `pipe`/`open`/socket
in this heavily threaded process, so a second close of the same number could close another camera's pipe.

The old "a reader is still alive, return" check is gone on purpose: each pipe now has its own reader, and an old
reader exits by itself at its own EOF. With the check, a restart while the old reader was still draining left the
new pipe without a reader, and ffmpeg blocked once the 64 KiB pipe buffer filled (recording included).

with exactly this content. `build()` only constructs objects; the lifecycle tests stub `CameraRecorder.start/stop`;

```python
"""Frame tap wiring: StreamIngestor, CameraRecorder, AppRuntime, DetectorRunner and serve.

Every camera has its own FrameTapDispatcher on ``CameraRuntime.dispatcher``, created before
its recorder. Only the proxy stream's ingestor carries the tap. The dispatcher holds that
camera's runner (one worker, short queue), then the ``--frame-consumer`` consumers. Nothing
here spawns ffmpeg: ``build()`` only constructs objects, and the lifecycle tests stub
``CameraRecorder.start`` / ``stop``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import cv2
import numpy as np
import pytest
from typer.testing import CliRunner

import rtsp_warden.cli as cli_mod
import rtsp_warden.db.bootstrap as bootstrap_mod
from rtsp_warden.app import AppRuntime, CameraRuntime
from rtsp_warden.config import (
    AppConfig,
    CameraConfig,
    ProxyConfig,
    RecordConfig,
    RuntimeConfig,
)
from rtsp_warden.consumers.motion_demo import MotionHeuristicConsumer
from rtsp_warden.detectors.registry import DetectorSpec
from rtsp_warden.detectors.runner import DetectorRunner
from rtsp_warden.frame_tap import FrameConsumer, FrameTapDispatcher
from rtsp_warden.recorder import CameraRecorder, StreamIngestor

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


class StubConsumer(FrameConsumer):
    name: str = "stub"

    def on_frame(self, camera: str, stream: str, jpeg_bytes: bytes, ts_unix: float) -> None:
        pass


def _jpeg() -> bytes:
    ok, buf = cv2.imencode(".jpg", np.zeros((48, 64, 3), dtype=np.uint8))
    assert ok
    return buf.tobytes()


def _cam(
    name: str,
    tmp_path: Path,
    *,
    sub: bool = False,
    record: bool = True,
    proxy: bool = False,
    port: int = 9001,
    motion: bool = False,
) -> CameraConfig:
    """Camera on rtsp://u:p@h/<name>[/sub]; MJPEG proxy only when ``proxy`` is True."""
    return CameraConfig(
        name=name,
        main_url=f"rtsp://u:p@h/{name}",
        sub_url=f"rtsp://u:p@h/{name}/sub" if sub else None,
        record=RecordConfig(enabled=record, output_dir=tmp_path / "rec"),
        proxy=ProxyConfig(enabled=proxy, port=port),
        detectors=[DetectorSpec(type="motion")] if motion else [],
    )


def _runtime(cams: list[CameraConfig], **kwargs: Any) -> AppRuntime:
    """A built AppRuntime (objects only; build() starts nothing)."""
    runtime = AppRuntime(cfg=AppConfig(cameras=cams, runtime=RuntimeConfig()), **kwargs)
    runtime.build()
    return runtime


def _rt(runtime: AppRuntime, name: str) -> CameraRuntime:
    rt = runtime.find_camera(name)
    assert rt is not None
    return rt


def _only_runner(rt: CameraRuntime) -> DetectorRunner:
    consumers = tuple(rt.dispatcher.consumers)
    assert len(consumers) == 1
    runner = consumers[0]
    assert isinstance(runner, DetectorRunner)
    return runner


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# StreamIngestor and CameraRecorder fields
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_stream_ingestor_has_frame_tap_fields() -> None:
    """StreamIngestor carries the tap flag, fps, width and dispatcher."""
    ingestor = StreamIngestor(
        camera_name="test",
        stream_name="main",
        upstream_url="rtsp://example.com/main",
        runtime=RuntimeConfig(),
    )
    assert ingestor.frame_tap_enabled is False
    assert ingestor.frame_tap_fps == 5.0
    assert ingestor.frame_tap_scale_width == 320
    assert ingestor.frame_tap_dispatcher is None
    assert ingestor.frame_tap_write_fd is None

    dispatcher = FrameTapDispatcher()
    ingestor2 = StreamIngestor(
        camera_name="test2",
        stream_name="sub",
        upstream_url="rtsp://example.com/sub",
        runtime=RuntimeConfig(),
        frame_tap_enabled=True,
        frame_tap_fps=10,
        frame_tap_scale_width=160,
        frame_tap_dispatcher=dispatcher,
    )
    assert ingestor2.frame_tap_enabled is True
    assert ingestor2.frame_tap_fps == 10
    assert ingestor2.frame_tap_scale_width == 160
    assert ingestor2.frame_tap_dispatcher is dispatcher


def test_camera_recorder_accepts_dispatcher(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    dispatcher = FrameTapDispatcher(consumers=[StubConsumer()])
    recorder = CameraRecorder(
        camera=_cam("c", tmp_path, sub=True),
        runtime=RuntimeConfig(),
        frame_tap_dispatcher=dispatcher,
    )
    assert recorder.frame_tap_dispatcher is dispatcher
    assert recorder.frame_tap_required is False


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CameraRecorder: the tap rides on the proxy stream only
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_tap_rides_on_the_sub_stream_when_the_proxy_reads_sub(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    cam = _cam("c", tmp_path, sub=True)
    assert cam.proxy.stream == "sub"
    dispatcher = FrameTapDispatcher()

    rec = CameraRecorder(camera=cam, runtime=RuntimeConfig(), frame_tap_dispatcher=dispatcher)

    assert rec.main is not None and rec.sub is not None
    assert rec.sub.frame_tap_enabled is True
    assert rec.sub.frame_tap_dispatcher is dispatcher
    assert rec.main.frame_tap_enabled is False
    assert rec.main.frame_tap_dispatcher is None


def test_tap_follows_an_explicit_proxy_stream_main(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    cam = _cam("c", tmp_path, sub=True)
    cam.proxy.stream = "main"
    dispatcher = FrameTapDispatcher()

    rec = CameraRecorder(camera=cam, runtime=RuntimeConfig(), frame_tap_dispatcher=dispatcher)

    assert rec.main is not None and rec.sub is not None
    assert rec.main.frame_tap_enabled is True
    assert rec.sub.frame_tap_enabled is False


def test_main_only_camera_taps_main(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    cam = _cam("c", tmp_path)
    assert cam.proxy.stream == "main"

    rec = CameraRecorder(
        camera=cam, runtime=RuntimeConfig(), frame_tap_dispatcher=FrameTapDispatcher()
    )

    assert rec.sub is None
    assert rec.main is not None
    assert rec.main.frame_tap_enabled is True


def test_no_dispatcher_means_no_tap(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    rec = CameraRecorder(camera=_cam("c", tmp_path, sub=True), runtime=RuntimeConfig())

    assert rec.main is not None and rec.sub is not None
    assert rec.main.frame_tap_enabled is False
    assert rec.sub.frame_tap_enabled is False


def test_the_tap_alone_creates_an_ingestor_only_when_required(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    cam = _cam("c", tmp_path, record=False, proxy=False)

    idle = CameraRecorder(
        camera=cam, runtime=RuntimeConfig(), frame_tap_dispatcher=FrameTapDispatcher()
    )
    wanted = CameraRecorder(
        camera=cam,
        runtime=RuntimeConfig(),
        frame_tap_dispatcher=FrameTapDispatcher(),
        frame_tap_required=True,
    )

    assert idle.frame_tap_required is False
    assert idle.main is None
    assert not idle.has_any()  # a camera nothing consumes spawns no ffmpeg
    assert wanted.main is not None
    assert wanted.main.frame_tap_enabled is True
    assert wanted.main.mjpeg_hub is None
    assert wanted.main.rtsp_publish_url is None
    assert wanted.main.record_cfg is not None
    assert wanted.main.record_cfg.enabled is False


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# AppRuntime.build: one dispatcher per camera, holding exactly its runner
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_build_gives_each_camera_its_own_dispatcher(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    runtime = _runtime(
        [
            _cam("a", tmp_path, sub=True, motion=True),
            _cam("b", tmp_path, motion=True),
            _cam("c", tmp_path),
        ]
    )
    a, b, c = runtime.cameras

    assert len({id(a.dispatcher), id(b.dispatcher), id(c.dispatcher)}) == 3
    for rt in (a, b, c):
        assert rt.recorder.frame_tap_dispatcher is rt.dispatcher
    runner_a, runner_b = _only_runner(a), _only_runner(b)
    assert runner_a.name == "detector_a" and runner_a.camera == "a"
    assert runner_b.name == "detector_b" and runner_b.camera == "b"
    assert tuple(c.dispatcher.consumers) == ()
    assert [r.name for r in runtime.detector_runners] == ["detector_a", "detector_b"]

    # The tap rides on the proxy stream only: sub for a, main for b and c.
    assert a.recorder.sub is not None and a.recorder.sub.frame_tap_enabled is True
    assert a.recorder.main is not None and a.recorder.main.frame_tap_enabled is False
    assert b.recorder.main is not None and b.recorder.main.frame_tap_enabled is True
    assert c.recorder.main is not None and c.recorder.main.frame_tap_enabled is True
    assert a.recorder.sub.frame_tap_dispatcher is a.dispatcher


def test_runtime_runners_use_one_worker_and_a_short_queue(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    runtime = _runtime([_cam("a", tmp_path, motion=True)])

    runner = _only_runner(runtime.cameras[0])

    assert runner.worker_count == 1
    assert runner.queue_maxsize == 8


def test_a_frame_reaches_only_its_own_cameras_runner(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    runtime = _runtime([_cam("a", tmp_path, motion=True), _cam("b", tmp_path, motion=True)])
    a, b = runtime.cameras
    runner_a, runner_b = _only_runner(a), _only_runner(b)

    # What b's tap reader thread does for every frame (runners not set up: no workers).
    b.dispatcher.dispatch(camera="b", stream="main", jpeg_bytes=_jpeg(), ts_unix=1.0)

    assert runner_a.status()["queue_size"] == 0
    assert runner_b.status()["queue_size"] == 1


def test_frame_consumers_join_every_cameras_dispatcher(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    stub = StubConsumer()
    runtime = _runtime(
        [_cam("a", tmp_path, motion=True), _cam("b", tmp_path, record=False)],
        frame_consumers=(stub,),
    )
    a, b = runtime.cameras

    consumers_a = tuple(a.dispatcher.consumers)
    assert [getattr(c, "name", None) for c in consumers_a] == ["detector_a", "stub"]
    assert consumers_a[1] is stub
    assert tuple(b.dispatcher.consumers) == (stub,)
    # b records nothing and serves no proxy, but the consumer wants its frames.
    assert b.recorder.main is not None and b.recorder.main.frame_tap_enabled is True


def test_a_camera_nothing_consumes_spawns_no_ingestor(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    runtime = _runtime([_cam("c", tmp_path, record=False, proxy=False)])

    rt = runtime.cameras[0]

    assert not rt.recorder.has_any()
    assert tuple(rt.dispatcher.consumers) == ()


def test_no_detectors_flag_builds_no_runner(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    runtime = _runtime([_cam("a", tmp_path, motion=True)], detectors_enabled=False)

    rt = runtime.cameras[0]

    assert runtime.detector_runners == []
    assert tuple(rt.dispatcher.consumers) == ()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# rebuild_camera_detectors: swaps the runner on that camera's dispatcher only
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_rebuild_without_detectors_unwires_the_runner(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    runtime = _runtime([_cam("a", tmp_path, motion=True), _cam("b", tmp_path, motion=True)])
    a, b = runtime.cameras
    runner_b = _only_runner(b)
    a.camera.detectors[0].enabled = False

    runtime.rebuild_camera_detectors("a")

    assert tuple(a.dispatcher.consumers) == ()
    assert [r.name for r in runtime.detector_runners] == ["detector_b"]
    assert _only_runner(b) is runner_b


def test_rebuild_swaps_in_a_running_runner_and_keeps_frame_consumers(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    stub = StubConsumer()
    runtime = _runtime([_cam("a", tmp_path, motion=True)], frame_consumers=(stub,))
    rt = runtime.cameras[0]
    old = tuple(rt.dispatcher.consumers)[0]

    runtime.rebuild_camera_detectors("a")
    try:
        consumers = tuple(rt.dispatcher.consumers)
        new = consumers[0]
        assert isinstance(new, DetectorRunner)
        assert new is not old
        assert consumers[1:] == (stub,)
        assert runtime.detector_runners == [new]
        assert new.queue_maxsize == 8
        assert new.status()["worker_count"] == 1  # set up before it was wired in
    finally:
        for runner in runtime.detector_runners:
            runner.teardown()


def test_rebuild_of_an_unknown_camera_raises(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    runtime = _runtime([_cam("a", tmp_path)])

    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="camera 'nope' not found"):
        runtime.rebuild_camera_detectors("nope")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Lifecycle requests (RW-0): restart builds a new dispatcher and rewires it
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


@pytest.fixture
def no_processes(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setattr(CameraRecorder, "start", lambda self: None)
    monkeypatch.setattr(CameraRecorder, "stop", lambda self: None)


@pytest.mark.usefixtures("no_processes")
def test_restart_rewires_the_new_cameras_dispatcher(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    runtime = _runtime([_cam("a", tmp_path, motion=True)])
    old = _rt(runtime, "a")
    old_runner = _only_runner(old)

    fut = runtime.request_restart_camera("a")
    runtime._drain_requests()
    try:
        assert fut.result(timeout=0) is None
        new = _rt(runtime, "a")
        assert new is not old
        assert new.dispatcher is not old.dispatcher
        assert new.recorder.frame_tap_dispatcher is new.dispatcher
        assert new.recorder.main is not None
        assert new.recorder.main.frame_tap_dispatcher is new.dispatcher
        new_runner = _only_runner(new)
        assert new_runner is not old_runner
        assert new_runner.camera == "a"
        assert runtime.detector_runners == [new_runner]
    finally:
        for runner in runtime.detector_runners:
            runner.teardown()


@pytest.mark.usefixtures("no_processes")
def test_remove_unwires_the_cameras_dispatcher(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    runtime = _runtime([_cam("a", tmp_path, motion=True), _cam("b", tmp_path, motion=True)])
    b = _rt(runtime, "b")

    fut = runtime.request_remove_camera("b")
    runtime._drain_requests()

    assert fut.result(timeout=0) is None
    assert tuple(b.dispatcher.consumers) == ()
    assert [r.name for r in runtime.detector_runners] == ["detector_a"]
    assert _only_runner(_rt(runtime, "a")).camera == "a"

def test_runner_ignores_frames_for_other_cameras_and_streams() -> None:
    runner = DetectorRunner(worker_count=0, queue_maxsize=8, camera="a", stream="main")

    runner.on_frame("b", "main", _jpeg(), 1.0)
    runner.on_frame("a", "sub", _jpeg(), 1.0)
    assert runner.status()["queue_size"] == 0

    runner.on_frame("a", "main", _jpeg(), 1.0)
    assert runner.status()["queue_size"] == 1


def test_runner_without_camera_or_stream_accepts_every_frame() -> None:
    runner = DetectorRunner(worker_count=0, queue_maxsize=8)

    runner.on_frame("a", "main", _jpeg(), 1.0)
    runner.on_frame("b", "sub", _jpeg(), 1.0)

    assert runner.camera is None and runner.stream is None
    assert runner.status()["queue_size"] == 2

SERVE_CONFIG = """cameras:
  - name: a
    main_url: rtsp://u:p@h/a
    record:
      enabled: false
    proxy:
      enabled: false
  - name: b
    main_url: rtsp://u:p@h/b
    record:
      enabled: false
    proxy:
      enabled: false
"""


def test_serve_adds_each_frame_consumer_to_every_camera(
    tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    (tmp_path / "config.yaml").write_text(SERVE_CONFIG)
    monkeypatch.chdir(tmp_path)
    started: list[AppRuntime] = []
    monkeypatch.setattr(cli_mod, "_require_binaries", lambda cfg: None)
    monkeypatch.setattr(bootstrap_mod, "bootstrap_database", lambda create_admin: None)
    monkeypatch.setattr(AppRuntime, "start", lambda self: started.append(self))
    monkeypatch.setattr(AppRuntime, "run_forever", lambda self: None)
    monkeypatch.setattr(AppRuntime, "stop_all", lambda self: None)

    result = CliRunner().invoke(
        cli_mod.app,
        ["serve", "-c", str(tmp_path / "config.yaml"), "--no-web", "--frame-consumer", "demo"],
    )

    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
    (runtime,) = started
    (consumer,) = runtime.frame_consumers
    assert isinstance(consumer, MotionHeuristicConsumer)
    assert [rt.camera.name for rt in runtime.cameras] == ["a", "b"]
    for rt in runtime.cameras:
        assert tuple(rt.dispatcher.consumers) == (consumer,)
        assert rt.dispatcher.consumers[0] is consumer
        assert rt.recorder.main is not None
        assert rt.recorder.main.frame_tap_enabled is True
```

```python
    def on_frame(self, camera: str, stream: str, jpeg_bytes: bytes, ts_unix: float) -> None:
```
