(c) Lines 338-365: replace everything from the heading line `### Detection` up to, but not including, the heading
line `### ONVIF` (on master: the `### Detection` section with its "chain of `FrameConsumer` objects" paragraph, the
5-row detector table, **Tuning per camera** and **Hot reload**, then the whole `### Alerts` section with the
`AlertManager` paragraph and the notifier-type list, and the blank line before `### ONVIF`) with:

````markdown
### Detection

Each camera's preview stream (`proxy.stream`; the main stream when there is no `sub_url`) also feeds the detectors: ffmpeg writes JPEG frames at the camera's `detect_fps` (default 5, from 0.5 to 30), scaled to the widest model input (at least 320 px), into a pipe read by that camera's detector runner. The runner works on one thread with a small queue; when inference is slower than the frame rate it drops the oldest queued frame and counts it, so overload means fewer samples, never growing memory.

| Detector | What | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `onnx` | YOLOX on ONNX Runtime, 80 COCO classes | The object detector. `model: yolox-s` (default, 640 px input, about 34 MB) or `yolox-nano` (416 px, about 3.5 MB, for small CPUs) |
| `motion` | MOG2 background subtraction | Very cheap. Its events are stored only when no `onnx` detector is enabled, or with `events: true` |
| `custom` | Your class via `import_path: module:Class` | Implements the `Detector` protocol (see Architecture invariants) |
| `person`, `vehicle`, `dnn` | HOG, Haar cascade, YOLOv4-tiny | Deprecated: each logs a warning naming `onnx`, and they are removed in the next release |

**Rates.** `detect_fps` is how many frames per second the camera's detectors receive. Changing it restarts that camera's ingest, because it is an ffmpeg argument (the Detection panel says so next to its Save button). A detector can run slower with its own `fps`, at most `detect_fps`; the runner skips frames for it. Expected cost at 2 fps with YOLOX-s: 10 to 15 ms per frame on an RTX 4080-class GPU, 60 to 120 ms on one modern CPU core.

**Models.** `yolox-s` and `yolox-nano` ship as descriptors inside the package. Their `.onnx` files are downloaded on first use into `runtime.models_dir` (default: `$WARDEN_MODELS_DIR`, else `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/rtsp-warden/models`, else `~/.cache/rtsp-warden/models`) and checked against a pinned SHA-256. Without internet access the camera keeps recording, its Detection panel shows the error, and the download is retried every 5 minutes; you can also copy the file to `<models_dir>/yolox-s/yolox_s.onnx` by hand. To add your own YOLOX-family model, create `<models_dir>/<name>/model.yaml` and set `model: <name>`:

```yaml
name: my-yolox
file: my_yolox.onnx          # in the same directory
labels: labels.txt           # one label per line; line number = class id
input_size: [640, 640]       # width, height (multiples of 32)
postprocess: yolox           # the only supported value
sha256: <64 hex characters>  # optional
url: https://example.com/my_yolox.onnx   # optional: downloaded when the file is missing
```

**Device.** `device: auto` (the default) uses CUDA when the GPU build of ONNX Runtime can load it, else the CPU. `cuda` asks for the GPU and falls back to the CPU with a warning badge on the camera. `cpu` never touches CUDA. The log names the provider in use once the model is loaded:

```
onnx detector onnx (model yolox-s, device auto) provider: CUDAExecutionProvider
```

**Classes and tuning per camera:**
- `detect_classes` — model labels to keep (for YOLOX, COCO names such as `person`, `car`, `dog`, `cat`); omit it for all labels. Unknown names fail config validation with the list of valid ones. The detection classes page offers "all" or a custom list.
- `min_confidence` per `onnx` detector — when unset it comes from `sensitivity` (0.5 at 50).
- `sensitivity` (0-100) — single knob that also scales the motion detector's threshold. Higher = more sensitive.
- `enabled` per detector — toggle individual detectors on/off without deleting config. The web UI identifies a detector by its position in `detectors:` and writes back only that entry, so other keys and `${VAR}` references survive.
- **Zones** — grid zones of N×M cells. `kind: ignore` (the default) drops detections whose box centre is in a blocked cell. `kind: area` never drops anything: its active (not blocked) cells form a named area, and an event's `zone` is the first `area` zone that contains the centre of its best box. Cells map onto the frame the detectors actually see, whatever the zone's saved `frame_width`/`frame_height`. A detector also accepts a polygon `roi`; a detection must pass the `roi` and every `ignore` zone.

**Hot reload:** web UI saves write `config.yaml`. A detector `enabled` toggle rebuilds that camera's detectors at once; sensitivity and detection classes rebuild when saved with "Save and reload"; zones rebuild from the zones page's reload button. `POST /cameras/{name}/reload` rebuilds from the in-memory config; it does not re-read the YAML, so hand edits still need a restart. A rebuild restarts the tracker empty, and restarts the camera's ingest only when the frame-tap settings change (`detect_fps`, or a model with another input width).

**Live boxes:** the "show boxes" switch next to the camera's live preview (off by default, remembered per browser) streams `/cameras/{name}/live-boxes.mjpeg`, with the tracker's current boxes drawn.

**Status:** the camera card and the `/health` page show the provider in use (`CUDAExecutionProvider` or `CPUExecutionProvider`), a warning when CUDA was requested but not used or a model failed to load, and processed / dropped frame counts. `/status.json` and `rtsp-warden status` carry the same values per camera.

### Events

Boxes from object detectors are matched across frames by a per-camera tracker (intersection over union, per label). A track that is matched on `min_track_frames` frames in a row (default 2) becomes one row in the `events` table: camera, label, best confidence, zone, and a JPEG thumbnail of the best frame with its box drawn (`<output_dir>/<camera>/thumbnails/<event_id>.jpg`). While the object stays in view, the row and thumbnail are updated when a better frame arrives (at most once per second). Once the tracker has not seen the object for `track_grace_seconds` (default 3), the event gets its end time. Two people walking past are two events; a person standing still for ten minutes is one.

Motion makes one event per burst (it opens after `min_track_frames` frames with motion and ends after `track_grace_seconds` without), with no thumbnail, and only when the camera has no enabled `onnx` detector or the motion detector sets `events: true`.

The Events page shows cards (thumbnail, label, confidence, camera, zone, time) with filters for camera, label and date; an event's page shows the full thumbnail, its clip and every action run. Events made with "Fire test event" carry a **test** badge.

### Rules and actions

Actions are named notification targets in the top-level `actions:` list. Rules are per camera and decide which events reach which actions. A complete example (the test suite validates it):

<!-- config-example: detection-example -->
```yaml
cameras:
  - name: yard
    main_url: rtsp://${CAM_USER}:${CAM_PASS}@192.168.1.60:554/stream1
    detect_fps: 5
    detectors:
      - type: motion
        fps: 5
      - type: onnx
        model: yolox-s
        device: auto
        fps: 2
        min_confidence: 0.5
    zones:
      - name: driveway
        kind: area
        grid_cols: 2
        grid_rows: 2
        frame_width: 1920
        frame_height: 1080
        blocked_cells: [[1, 0], [1, 1]]   # the driveway is the left half
      - name: road
        kind: ignore
        grid_cols: 2
        grid_rows: 2
        frame_width: 1920
        frame_height: 1080
        blocked_cells: [[0, 0], [1, 0]]   # ignore the top half (the road)
    rules:
      - name: person-any-time
        labels: [person]
        zones: []                 # empty = any zone
        min_confidence: 0.6
        between: null             # or "22:00-06:00", local time, may wrap midnight
        cooldown_seconds: 60
        clip: true
        actions: [phone]
      - name: car-in-driveway-at-night
        labels: [car]
        zones: [driveway]
        between: "22:00-06:00"
        actions: [phone, homeassistant]

actions:
  - name: phone
    type: ntfy
    url: https://ntfy.sh
    topic: warden-home            # ntfy.sh topics are public: pick a long random name
    token: ${NTFY_TOKEN}          # optional
  - name: homeassistant
    type: webhook
    url: http://ha.local:8123/api/webhook/warden

runtime:
  public_url: http://nvr.lan:8080   # base of the links in notifications
```

A rule matches an event when its label is in `labels` (empty = any), its zone is in `zones` (empty = any; the names must be `area` zones of that camera), its confidence is at least `min_confidence`, and the local time is inside `between` (`"HH:MM-HH:MM"`, may wrap midnight; the server's time zone, `TZ` in Docker). Rules are evaluated when the event opens, so notifications are prompt. For `cooldown_seconds` after a rule fired for a camera and label, further matches are recorded on the event (`suppressed_by` in its metadata) but send nothing. Unknown action or zone names in a rule are config errors, and so are labels that none of the camera's `onnx` models know (`motion` is always allowed).

Every action gets the same payload: `camera`, `label`, `confidence`, `zone`, `started_at`, `ended_at` (null while the event is open), `thumbnail_url`, `clip_url` (null until a clip exists), `event_url` and `test`. The URLs are absolute. Set `runtime.public_url` to the address you open the web UI with from your phone; without it they are built from the web UI's bind address, with `0.0.0.0` shown as `localhost`, which only works on the server itself.

| Type | Fields | What it sends |
|---|---|---|
| `ntfy` | `url`, `topic`, `token` (optional) | A push with the thumbnail attached; the token goes in the `Authorization` header |
| `webhook` | `url`, `method` (`POST` or `PUT`), `headers` | The payload as JSON |
| `apprise` | `urls` (a list of [Apprise URLs](https://github.com/caronc/apprise/wiki)) | Title and text with the thumbnail attached: email, Discord, Telegram, Slack, MQTT and 90+ more |

Each run is stored in `action_runs` and shown on the event's page and, as last run and failure count, on the Actions page. Failed runs are not retried. Keep secrets in the environment: `token: ${NTFY_TOKEN}` in `config.yaml` and `NTFY_TOKEN=...` in `.env`; with Docker, also pass it to the container under `environment:` in `docker-compose.yml` (`NTFY_TOKEN: ${NTFY_TOKEN}`).

**Testing.** The Actions page has a **Test** button per action that sends a synthetic payload straight through that action and shows the result (it writes no `action_runs` row). On a camera's Detection panel, **Fire test event** creates a real `person` event (type `test`, placeholder thumbnail), runs it through that camera's rules with cooldowns ignored and through the action queue, and lists the rules that matched; it never makes a clip.

````

(d) Lines 373-375: replace everything from the heading line `### Clips` up to, but not including, the heading line

detection event. ... are tracked in the `clips` table.", and a blank line; if Task 7 reworded the paragraph, replace

````markdown
### Clips

A rule with `clip: true` makes a clip when its event ends: the recorded `.ts` segments from `clips.pre_seconds` before the event started to `clips.post_seconds` after it ended (capped at `clips.max_duration` seconds) are joined without re-encoding and remuxed to `<output_dir>/<camera>/clips/<event_id>.mp4`. If the MP4 remux fails (some camera streams do not survive it), the joined `.ts` is kept and played through the HLS player instead. The job waits until `post_seconds` (plus two seconds) have passed after the end, so the last segment is complete. The camera must record (`record.enabled: true`); notifications go out when the event opens, so they never carry a clip link. The event's page plays the clip.

## Upgrading from 1.3

- **Python 3.11 or newer** is required (ONNX Runtime ships no Python 3.10 builds).
- **Database:** `serve` upgrades the schema when it starts. A SQLite database is first copied next to itself as `<file>.bak-<old revision>` (for example `warden.db.bak-0002_clips`); to go back to 1.3, stop rtsp-warden and put that copy back. With PostgreSQL, take a `pg_dump` before upgrading. A database written by a newer release is refused with a message and left untouched. Existing events keep their data and get their camera name from the old event text; the never-used `cameras`, `recordings` and `ingest_health` tables and the `clips` table are dropped.
- **Removed pages:** the recordings list and detail pages, the timeline, and the "Generate Clip" button. Segment files stay on disk under `<output_dir>/<camera>/<stream>/`. MP4s made by the old button stay where they were written (`clips.output_dir`, by default a `clips/` directory next to the recordings directory); delete them when you no longer need them.
- **Alerts are now actions:** the Alerts page is replaced by the Actions page. A legacy `alerts.notifiers` list still loads for this release: each `enabled: true` entry becomes an action with the same name (its `severities`, `min_interval_seconds`, `min_severity` and `title_template` are dropped, with a warning), `enabled: false` entries are ignored, and `alerts.enabled` no longer does anything. Nothing is sent until a camera rule names the action. Move the entries to `actions:` and add rules; a name used in both lists is a config error.
- **Deprecated, removed in the next release** (each logs one warning when the config loads): the detector types `person`, `vehicle` and `dnn` (use `type: onnx`), a detector's `interval_seconds` (converted to `fps = 1 / interval_seconds`, capped at the camera's `detect_fps`), and the top-level `alerts:` section.
- **`record.mode: event`:** detection cannot start an event-mode recording (see Recording); use `continuous` with retention.

````

(the last bullet of the `### Docker (recommended)` section) insert:

````markdown

Models are stored in `./data/models` (`WARDEN_MODELS_DIR` in `docker-compose.yml`), so they are downloaded once and survive image rebuilds. For an NVIDIA GPU, add the GPU overlay below.

### GPU (NVIDIA)

Without a GPU, YOLOX runs on the CPU (see Detection for the expected cost). To use an NVIDIA GPU:

**Docker.** Install the NVIDIA driver and the [NVIDIA Container Toolkit](https://docs.nvidia.com/datacenter/cloud-native/container-toolkit/latest/install-guide.html) on the host (`nvidia-smi` must work and report CUDA 13 or newer), then start with the GPU overlay. It builds `Dockerfile.cuda` (the slim image with `onnxruntime-gpu` and NVIDIA's CUDA 13 / cuDNN 9 Python wheels, a multi-gigabyte image) and reserves the GPU for the container:

```bash
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.gpu.yml up -d --build
docker compose logs warden | grep "provider:"
# onnx detector onnx (model yolox-s, device auto) provider: CUDAExecutionProvider
```

The line appears once the model is loaded (on the first frame when it still had to be downloaded). `CPUExecutionProvider` there means CUDA did not load: check `nvidia-smi` on the host and the container toolkit. With `device: cuda` the camera card also shows a warning badge.

**uv or pip on the host.** The CPU and GPU builds of ONNX Runtime install into the same Python package, so never let both into one environment. From a source checkout:

```bash
uv sync --extra gpu --no-install-package onnxruntime --reinstall-package onnxruntime-gpu
uv run --no-sync rtsp-warden serve -c config.yaml --web --web-port 8080
# a plain `uv run` reinstalls the CPU build; back to CPU: uv sync --reinstall-package onnxruntime
```

With pip: `pip install "rtsp-warden[gpu] @ git+https://github.com/Veedubin/RSTP-Warden.git"`, then `pip uninstall -y onnxruntime onnxruntime-gpu` and `pip install "onnxruntime-gpu[cuda,cudnn]>=1.28"`.

**systemd.** The shipped unit sets `PrivateDevices=true`, which hides `/dev/nvidia*` from the service. Run `sudo systemctl edit rtsp-warden`, add `[Service]` and `PrivateDevices=false`, and restart.

The NVIDIA libraries are under NVIDIA's own license. They come only with the `gpu` extra or the CUDA image; rtsp-warden itself stays MIT.
````

````markdown

## GPU (NVIDIA)

`Dockerfile.cuda` is `Dockerfile` with one change: the venv gets the `gpu` extra
(`uv sync --frozen --no-dev --extra gpu --no-install-package onnxruntime`), that is
`onnxruntime-gpu` plus NVIDIA's CUDA 13 and cuDNN 9 pip wheels, instead of the CPU `onnxruntime`.
There is no CUDA base image: the NVIDIA Container Toolkit injects the driver, everything else
comes from the wheels. The host needs the NVIDIA driver (`nvidia-smi` reports CUDA 13 or newer)
and the [NVIDIA Container Toolkit](https://docs.nvidia.com/datacenter/cloud-native/container-toolkit/latest/install-guide.html).

```bash
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.gpu.yml up -d --build
docker compose logs warden | grep "provider:"   # ... provider: CUDAExecutionProvider
docker compose exec warden python -c "from onnxruntime.capi import build_and_package_info as b; print(b.package_name)"   # onnxruntime-gpu
```

`onnxruntime.get_available_providers()` lists `CUDAExecutionProvider` whenever the GPU build is
installed, even when CUDA cannot load; trust the `provider:` log line. The distroless image stays
CPU-only (its library collector never looks inside the venv).
````

````markdown

## Detection models and GPU

The unit sets `WARDEN_MODELS_DIR=/var/lib/rtsp-warden/models`. The YOLOX model (about 34 MB) is
downloaded there on the first frame, so the first start needs internet access. Without it the
cameras still record and the download is retried every 5 minutes; you can also copy
`yolox_s.onnx` into `/var/lib/rtsp-warden/models/yolox-s/` by hand (owned by `rtsp-warden`). A
`WARDEN_MODELS_DIR=` line in `warden.env` overrides the unit's value.

The unit's `PrivateDevices=true` hides `/dev/nvidia*`, so detection runs on the CPU. To use an
NVIDIA GPU, install the GPU build of ONNX Runtime into the environment rtsp-warden runs from (see
the README's GPU section), then add a drop-in:

```bash
sudo systemctl edit rtsp-warden      # add these two lines, then save:
#   [Service]
#   PrivateDevices=false
sudo systemctl restart rtsp-warden
sudo journalctl -u rtsp-warden | grep "provider:"   # ... provider: CUDAExecutionProvider
```

The first start after upgrading from 1.3 also upgrades the database schema; a SQLite database is
copied to `warden.db.bak-<old revision>` in the same directory first.
````

(d) Lines 86-104: replace everything from the heading line that starts `### Detector pipeline` up to, but not
including, the heading line `### Web layer (\`web/\`)` (Task 2 already rewrote parts of it; replace whatever is
there) with:

````markdown
### Detector pipeline (`frame_tap.py` → `detectors/` → `actions/`)

```
CameraRuntime.dispatcher → DetectorRunner.on_frame (one per camera; queue 8, drop-oldest, 1 worker)
  → cv2.imdecode → apply_masks (privacy polygons) → for each DetectorSlot due at its own fps:
      Detector.process(frame_bgr, ts_unix) → filter_by_roi → ignore-zone GridMask.filter_detections
  → motion slots:  MotionBurst → EventSink (only when CameraConfig.motion_events_enabled)
  → tracked slots: Tracker (greedy IoU per label) → EventBuilder → events row + thumbnail
      → on open:  RuleEngine.evaluate → ActionQueue (one action_runs row per run)
      → on close: ClipScheduler (when a matched rule has clip: true)
```

The `Detector` protocol (`detectors/base.py`) is `name`, `kind`, `setup()`,
`process(frame_bgr, ts_unix) -> list[Detection]` (bbox is x, y, w, h in frame pixels),
`teardown()`. `DetectorType` is `motion | person | vehicle | dnn | custom | onnx`; `person`,
`vehicle`, `dnn` and a spec's `interval_seconds` are deprecated and warn once through
`deprecations.warn_once`. `onnx` is `OnnxDetector` (`detectors/builtin/onnx.py`): YOLOX on ONNX
Runtime, providers chosen from `device` (`auto | cuda | cpu`), and the log line
`... provider: CUDAExecutionProvider` (or `CPUExecutionProvider`). It imports `onnxruntime` and
fetches its model only when it loads (in `setup()` when the file is present, else on the first
frame), never in `__init__`, so `rtsp-warden status` stays offline. A failed load sets `error`,
returns no detections and retries every 300 s of frame time; recording is never affected. Models
come from `detectors/model_registry.py`: built-in descriptors in `detectors/models/` (`yolox-s`,
`yolox-nano`, `coco.txt`), user descriptors in `runtime.models_dir` (`WARDEN_MODELS_DIR`, else the
XDG cache), SHA-256-verified downloads, and only `postprocess: yolox`. `detect_classes` and
`rules[].labels` are validated against the camera's model labels when the config loads.

`build_detectors_for_camera(cam, specs, *, models_dir)` is the single entry point: it applies
camera `sensitivity` and `detect_classes`, turns `kind: ignore` zones into `GridMask`s (normalised
by the decoded frame size, not the zone's saved size) and `kind: area` zones into the named masks
that set `event.zone`, and returns one `DetectorSlot` per spec. The slot index is the spec's list
position, which is also the detector's identity in the web UI and in config write-back
(`_persist_detector_entry`). The frame tap's rate and width come from
`config.compute_tap_settings(cam)`: `detect_fps`, and the widest enabled model input (min 320).

Hot reload is `AppRuntime.rebuild_camera_detectors(name)`: it rebuilds the bundle from the
in-memory `CameraConfig`, sets the new runner up, swaps it under `_detector_lock` onto that
camera's own dispatcher, then tears the old runner down (which closes its open events). The
tracker starts empty. When the required tap settings changed (`detect_fps`, or a model of another
input width) it calls `request_restart_camera(name)` instead, because they are ffmpeg arguments.

````

(f) Lines 140-151: replace everything from the heading line `### Database (\`db/\`)` up to, but not including, the
heading line `### Alerts and ONVIF` with:

```markdown
### Database (`db/`)

`db/engine.py` resolves `WARDEN_DB_URL` (default SQLite under `$XDG_DATA_HOME`) into
a process-wide engine; `reset_engine()` is how tests swap databases. `db/schema.py` is
both the CRUD helper layer and `ensure_schema()`: an empty DB is upgraded to head, a legacy
`create_all` DB is stamped, a DB behind head is upgraded (a SQLite file is first copied to
`<db>.bak-<revision>`), and an unknown revision stops startup. `serve` runs it inside
`bootstrap_database()` before any thread starts.

Tables at `0003_detection_events`: `users`, `sessions`, `api_tokens`, `events`, `action_runs`
(plus `alembic_version`); `cameras`, `recordings`, `ingest_health` and `clips` were dropped.
`events` stores `camera_name` directly (0003 backfilled it from the old message text), plus
`label`, `confidence`, `zone`, `track_id`, `ended_at`, `thumbnail_path` and `clip_path` (both
relative to the camera's `record.output_dir`); `event_type = "test"` marks "Fire test event" rows.
Datetimes are written as naive UTC and read back through `schema.as_utc()`. Use the helpers
(`insert_event`, `update_event`, `close_event`, `list_events(camera_name=..., label=..., since=...,
until=...)`, `insert_action_run`, `action_stats`) rather than raw sessions. Thumbnails live at
`<output_dir>/<camera>/thumbnails/<event_id>.jpg` and clips at
`<output_dir>/<camera>/clips/<event_id>.(mp4|ts)`; retention sweeps both by age and size, and
`keep_last_n` counts only `main/` and `sub/` segments.

```

(g) Lines 153-160 (the heading and the first paragraph of the alerts section; stop before the blank line 161, so the
ONVIF paragraph at 162-165, which RW-2 edits, keeps its own lines). Replace

```markdown
### Alerts and ONVIF

`AlertManager` is constructed in `create_app` when `cfg.alerts.enabled` and builds its
notifiers in `__init__`; it is used by the `/alerts` admin routes (list, edit, and the
`POST /alerts/{name}/test` button). `dispatch_event` has no caller in the runtime path:
`EventSink` does not call it, and the ONVIF subscriber callback registered by
`/onvif/cameras/{name}/events/subscribe` only logs. Wiring detections to notifiers is
sub-project 3 in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-02-detection-and-automation-design.md`.
```

with

```markdown
### Actions, rules and ONVIF

`actions/` replaced `alerts/` (there is no `AlertManager`). Top-level `actions:` entries (`ntfy`,
`webhook`, `apprise`) are built by `actions/factory.build_actions(cfg)`. Every action is
synchronous (`send(payload, attachment) -> ActionResult`, `test() -> ActionResult`), creates its
own `httpx.Client` per call, and never puts URLs, topics or tokens into `ActionResult.error`.
Per-camera `rules:` are evaluated by `actions/rules.RuleEngine` when an event opens (label, area
zone, `min_confidence`, local-time `between` that may wrap midnight, cooldown keyed by camera, rule
and label). Matches are enqueued on `ActionQueue` (bounded at 256, drop-oldest, one daemon worker,
one `action_runs` row per run, no retries); a matched `clip: true` rule schedules a `ClipJob` on
`ClipScheduler`, which runs after `ended_at + clips.post_seconds + 2 s`, writes an MP4, and keeps
the joined `.ts` when the remux fails. Payload URLs use `runtime.public_url`, else the web bind
address with `0.0.0.0` / `::` shown as `localhost`. A legacy `alerts.notifiers` list is mapped onto
`actions` at load with one warning. ONVIF events received through
`/onvif/cameras/{name}/events/subscribe` are still only logged; they create no events.
```

### Task 19: Manual verification against the Foscam (gated on the owner's OK; never a gate)

**Purpose.** Run the finished `feat/detection` build once against the owner's real camera, end to end, the way a
home-lab user would: a hand-written `config.yaml` with `main_url` only, `detect_fps: 5`, an `onnx` detector
(`yolox-s`, `fps: 2`, `device: auto`) and one rule `person-any-time` that notifies an ntfy test topic and asks for a
clip. Spec section 12 ("Manual" bullet), section 10 (the provider log line), ruling R22. Tasks 1-18 pin every
behaviour offline with fakes. This task covers what fakes cannot:
- the real YOLOX download from GitHub and the SHA-256 pinned in Task 3, which was corroborated from mirrors but never
  computed from the GitHub bytes (Task 3 says this task confirms it);
- ONNX Runtime on the real CPU build and (optional) the real CUDA build on the owner's RTX 4080 SUPER;
- the frame tap's pipe in a real ffmpeg process (Task 2), the tap rate and width (R18);
- detection of a real person: one event per walk, one event for a minute of standing still (review focus 2), the
  box drawn on the right place in the thumbnail and the live preview;
- a real ntfy delivery with the thumbnail attached, the cooldown, and the "Test" / "Fire test event" buttons (R13);

**Paths used in every command.** Shell state does not persist between Bash calls, so commands spell them out.
- Worktree (WT): `/home/jcharles/Projects/python/rtsp-warden_v0.2.0/.worktrees/rw-3` (branch `feat/detection`).
- Scratch folder (S): `/home/jcharles/Projects/python/rtsp-warden_v0.2.0/.worktrees/rw3-foscam-scratch`. It sits
  outside both worktrees, inside the main checkout's `.worktrees/` directory, which RW-0 Task 0.1 made git-ignored.
  The config, the owner's `.env`, the test login, the database, the logs, the recordings, the thumbnails, the clips
  and the model file all live there. Nothing in it is ever added to git; Step 27 deletes it as the owner decides.
- Three small wrappers written in Step 4 keep the commands short and safe:
  `<S>/chk` runs the checker, `<S>/rw` runs `rtsp-warden` inside the scratch folder against the scratch database,
  `<S>/serve.sh RUN [admin]` runs `serve` and writes `<S>/serve-RUN.log`. All three use `uv run --no-sync`, because a
  syncing `uv run` would silently put the CPU onnxruntime back over the GPU build in Step 20 (gap-4 gotcha 5).
- Web UI: `http://127.0.0.1:8097` (RW-2 Task 12 uses 8098 and RW-2 Task 11 uses 8099). The camera's MJPEG side
  server is pinned to `127.0.0.1:9011` so it is not exposed on the LAN. A local "black hole" on `127.0.0.1:8199`
  accepts connections and never answers; it plays a stalled download in phase A.
- Camera: Foscam C1 V3 through the owner's port forward at `192.168.1.72` (RTSP 554). `videoMain` is H.264
  1280x720 at 15 fps; `videoSub` sends no video, so the config has `main_url` only and the proxy and frame tap read
  the main stream (`CameraConfig._fallback_proxy_stream`, `src/rtsp_warden/config.py:313-318` on master).
- Phases: A = `serve` run 1 with the model download stalled; B = run 2 with the real `yolox-s` on the CPU build (the
  walk-throughs); C = run 3 with `device: cuda` on the CPU build (fallback warning); D = run 4 on the GPU build
  (optional).

**Credential rules (binding for this task).**
- The agent never types, pastes, prints, logs or commits the Foscam user name or password, the ntfy topic or the ntfy
  token. The owner types them into `<S>/.env` with their own editor (Step 5). `config.yaml` only holds
  `${CAM_USER}`, `${CAM_PASS}`, `${NTFY_URL}`, `${NTFY_TOPIC}`, `${NTFY_TOKEN}` references, expanded at load
  (`expand_env`, `src/rtsp_warden/config.py:17-40`). On ntfy.sh a topic is effectively a password: anyone who knows it
  can read the messages.
- The app login is a throwaway test account (`admin` plus a generated password in `<S>/admin.env`, Step 3). The agent
  may type that password into the local login page (it is a test value of the app under test on 127.0.0.1). It never
  repeats it in chat. `db/bootstrap.py:48-53` logs it once in `serve-1.log`; the checker masks it.
- Never run commands that print secrets: `cat`, `less`, `grep` or `source` on `.env` (only `admin.env` is read, in
  Step 8, one line), `env`, `printenv`, `ps aux`, `ps -ef`, `pgrep -a`, `pgrep -l -f`, reads of `/proc/*/cmdline` or
  `/proc/*/environ` (ffmpeg's argv holds the expanded camera URL), or an unfiltered `cat`/`tail` of a serve log
  (httpx logs the ntfy URL with the topic, see K1). Read logs only through `<S>/chk log-tail` / `wait-log`, processes
  only through `<S>/chk procs` / `cpu` / `gpu`, and page text only through the masking snippets below.
- Ask in chat and wait for a clear yes before anything not covered by the Step 1 OK. Never push.

**Known risks recorded ahead of time** (each one is a defect when it shows; Step 23 lists the ones observed):
- K1 (verified while writing this plan): httpx logs every request at INFO, including the full URL, for example
  `HTTP Request: POST https://ntfy.example/<topic>?title=person+on+foscam-c1 "HTTP/1.1 200 OK"` (httpx 0.28.1,
  `httpx/_client.py:1025`, reproduced with `setup_logging("info")` from `src/rtsp_warden/logging_utils.py:18-36`,
  which quiets only `asyncio` and `urllib3` at lines 34-36). Every ntfy send therefore writes the topic into the
  serve log. It shows in Steps 18 and 21 as `serve-2.log: ... ntfy_topic=<n>`. Suspected fix site
  `src/rtsp_warden/logging_utils.py:34-36` (add `httpx` and `httpcore` at WARNING); that file is in neither track's
  ownership list, so the orchestrator assigns it.
- K2 (reasoned from code, not run): RW-3 Task 5's `OnnxDetector._reload_if_due` holds `self._lock` while
  `ensure_model_file` downloads (up to its 60 s timeout), and `OnnxDetector.teardown()` takes the same lock. Master's
  `AppRuntime.rebuild_camera_detectors` (`src/rtsp_warden/app.py:376-381`, `:390-395` and `:413-417`) tears the
  old runner down on the web request thread under `_detector_lock` (`DetectorRunner.teardown`,
  `src/rtsp_warden/detectors/runner.py:81-94`: join with a 5 s timeout, then `det.teardown()`). A detector toggle during a stalled download can then hang the request for up
  to about 60 s. Step 8 measures it. Suspected sites: Task 5's `teardown()`
  (`src/rtsp_warden/detectors/builtin/onnx.py`) and Task 2/12's rebuild path in `src/rtsp_warden/app.py`.
- K3 (reasoned): at `fps: 2` a brisk walk moves a person's box by about its own width between samples, so the IoU
  between consecutive boxes can fall below the tracker's 0.3 (spec 7.1) and one walk can become two or three events.
  Step 13 shows it as `person_events` above 1. Suspected site `src/rtsp_warden/detectors/tracking.py` (Task 6).
- K4 (spec 7.2 by design): rules fire on event open with the best confidence so far. With the rule's
  `min_confidence: 0.6` above the detector's 0.5, a person who enters at the frame edge can open an event below 0.6
  and get no notification although the event's final confidence is higher. Step 13 shows it as an event with no
  action run and no `suppressed_by`.
- K5 (verified on master while writing this plan, with the checker below and a dead camera URL): `/status.json`
  (no login) returns ffmpeg's raw `stderr_tail` (`src/rtsp_warden/cli.py:236-242`), which holds the expanded camera
  URL when ffmpeg cannot open the input (`GET /status.json [200]: camera_password=2 ... unredacted_userinfo=1`). This
  task never points the camera at a dead URL, so it shows only if the real connection fails during a run.

Continue with the next step when it does not depend on the failed one; otherwise jump to Step 21. Dependencies:

turns it into a fix task (systematic debugging, a failing offline test, the fix, the gate).

J1, the camera's Detection panel:
```js
(() => {
  const mask = (s) => s.replace(/(rtsps?:\/\/)[^\s@\/]*@/g, "$1<userinfo>@");
  const heads = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll("h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, summary, legend"));
  const head = heads.find((e) => /^\s*Detection\b/i.test(e.innerText || ""));
  const box = head ? head.closest("article, section, details, fieldset") || head.parentElement : null;
  const t = box ? box.innerText : "";
  const lines = t.split("\n").map((l) => l.trim()).filter(Boolean);
  const fps = box ? box.querySelector('[name="detect_fps"]') : null;
  const toggles = box
    ? Array.from(box.querySelectorAll("[hx-post*='/detectors/'], form[action*='/detectors/']")).map(
        (e) => e.getAttribute("hx-post") || e.getAttribute("action")
      )
    : [];
  return {
    panel_found: !!box,
    provider: (t.match(/(CUDA|CPU)ExecutionProvider/) || [null])[0],
    detect_fps_value: fps ? fps.value : null,
    restart_note: /restart/i.test(t),
    problem_lines: lines.filter((l) => /unavailable|error|failed|warning|requested|timed out/i.test(l)).map(mask).slice(0, 6),
    detector_lines: lines.filter((l) => /\b(onnx|motion)\b/i.test(l)).map(mask).slice(0, 6),
    rule_lines: lines.filter((l) => /person-any-time/.test(l)).map(mask).slice(0, 3),
    toggles: [...new Set(toggles)],
    buttons: box
      ? Array.from(box.querySelectorAll("button, input[type=submit]")).map((b) => (b.innerText || b.value || "").trim()).filter(Boolean).slice(0, 10)
      : [],
    text: mask(t).slice(0, 2000),
  };
})()
```

(() => {
  const t = document.body.innerText;
  const mask = (s) => s.replace(/(rtsps?:\/\/)[^\s@\/]*@/g, "$1<userinfo>@");
  const thumbs = Array.from(document.images).filter((i) => /\/events\/\d+\/thumbnail\.jpg/.test(i.getAttribute("src") || ""));

    event_links: [...new Set(links)].slice(0, 12),
    thumbnails: thumbs.length,
    thumbnails_loaded: thumbs.filter((i) => i.complete && i.naturalWidth > 0).length,
    percents: (t.match(/\b\d{1,3}\s?%/g) || []).slice(0, 12),
    has_person: /\bperson\b/i.test(t),
    has_test_badge: /\btest\b/i.test(t),
    has_expired: /expired/i.test(t),
    text: mask(t).slice(0, 1500),
  };
})()

J5, an event detail page (waits up to 8 s for the video's metadata):
```js
await (async () => {
  const mask = (s) => s.replace(/(rtsps?:\/\/)[^\s@\/]*@/g, "$1<userinfo>@");
  const rect = (el) => {
    const r = el.getBoundingClientRect();
    return [Math.round(r.left), Math.round(r.top), Math.round(r.right), Math.round(r.bottom)];
  };
  const thumb = Array.from(document.images).find((i) => /\/thumbnail\.jpg/.test(i.getAttribute("src") || ""));
  const v = document.querySelector("video");
  let video = null;
  if (v) {
    if (v.readyState < 1) {
      await new Promise((resolve) => {
        v.addEventListener("loadedmetadata", resolve, { once: true });
        setTimeout(resolve, 8000);
      });
    }
    video = {
      src: (v.currentSrc || v.getAttribute("src") || "").replace(location.origin, ""),
      ready_state: v.readyState,
      duration: Number.isFinite(v.duration) ? Math.round(v.duration * 10) / 10 : String(v.duration),
      error: v.error ? v.error.code : null,
      size: [v.videoWidth, v.videoHeight],
    };
  }
  const t = document.body.innerText;
  return {
    path: location.pathname,
    thumbnail_loaded: thumb ? thumb.complete && thumb.naturalWidth > 0 : null,
    thumbnail_px: thumb ? [thumb.naturalWidth, thumb.naturalHeight] : null,
    thumbnail_rect: thumb ? rect(thumb) : null,
    video,
    run_lines: t.split("\n").filter((l) => /\bphone\b/.test(l)).map(mask).slice(0, 5),
    test_badge: /\btest\b/i.test(t),
    text: mask(t).slice(0, 1500),
  };
})()
```

Create `/home/jcharles/Projects/python/rtsp-warden_v0.2.0/.worktrees/rw3-foscam-scratch/check_rw3_foscam.py` with
exactly this content. It was run while this plan was written against master `e5623cb` with fake values (a master
`serve` with a dead camera URL for `status`, `wait`, `procs`, `cpu`, `gpu`, `stop`, `leaks` and the login; a seeded
0002 database through master's migrations for `seed-0002` and `db`; a hand-built 0003-shaped database with real
JPEG thumbnails and an ffmpeg-made mp4 for `mark`, `visit`, `clip` and `cooldown-wait`; a fake `/status.json` plus a
process holding a real pipe for `tap`; an injected registry module for `model`). Every command behaved as described
below, and `leaks` caught master's K5 leak.
```python
"""RW-3 Task 19 checker: prints facts about the scratch run and never prints a secret.

Run with the worktree's environment from any directory (never let uv sync here):
    uv run --no-sync --project <WT> python <S>/check_rw3_foscam.py <command> [args]

Commands:
    env                        .env keys (set / empty / missing), file mode, camera URL parse check
    config                     facts from config.yaml as written (raw YAML, nothing expanded)
    seed-0002                  create warden.db at revision 0002_clips with one legacy motion row
    db                         schema revision vs head, tables, backups, the legacy row, row counts
    model [name]               model file facts and SHA-256 check (default yolox-s)
    status                     /status.json summary for the camera, including its detection block
    status-file PATH           the same summary from a saved `rtsp-warden status` JSON file
    tap                        frame-tap output of the running ingest: pipe fd, rate, scale filter
    wait STATE [sec]           poll /status.json until STATE: running | stopped (exit 1 on timeout)
    wait-log LOG TEXT [sec] [n]
                               poll <S>/<LOG> until TEXT is on n lines (default 1); print the
                               count and the last three matching lines, masked
    log-tail LOG [n]           last n lines (default 40) of <S>/<LOG>, masked
    segments [sec]             .ts segment facts, then again after <sec> seconds (default 20)
    procs                      ffmpeg processes on the camera, serve processes
    stop [sec]                 SIGINT to serve; wait up to <sec> (default 30) for it to exit
    cpu [sec]                  CPU use of serve and of the camera ffmpeg over <sec> (default 20)
    gpu                        whether the serve process holds GPU memory (nvidia-smi)
    mark NAME                  remember the newest event id and the time as NAME
    cooldown-wait SEC          sleep until SEC s after the newest notified person event opened
    visit NAME [sec]           events after mark NAME; wait up to <sec> (default 90) to settle
    clip ID [sec]              wait up to <sec> (default 120) for the event's clip, then ffprobe it
    leaks                      secret scan: logs, config, status-cli files, DB text, pages, JSON
    scan FILE                  secret scan of one file

Environment overrides (only for checking this script itself): CHECK_BASE (web UI base URL),
CHECK_SCRIPT_LOCATION (Alembic script location).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import html
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import signal
import sqlite3
import stat
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any
from urllib.parse import quote, unquote, urlsplit

import httpx
import yaml
from rtsp_warden.cli import _parse_dotenv_value

S = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
CAM = "foscam-c1"
BASE = os.environ.get("CHECK_BASE", "http://127.0.0.1:8097")
SCRIPT_LOCATION = os.environ.get("CHECK_SCRIPT_LOCATION", "rtsp_warden:migrations")
DB = S / "warden.db"
REC = S / "recordings"
MODELS = S / "models"
ENV_KEYS = ("CAM_USER", "CAM_PASS", "NTFY_URL", "NTFY_TOPIC", "NTFY_TOKEN")
CAM_URL_REF = "rtsp://${CAM_USER}:${CAM_PASS}@192.168.1.72:554/videoMain"
PAGES = (
    "/",
    "/cameras",
    f"/cameras/{CAM}",
    "/events",
    "/actions",
    "/health",
    "/health/partial",
    "/status.json",
    "/metrics",
)
USERINFO_RE = re.compile(r"rtsps?://([^\s/@\"'<>]+)@")
ALLOWED_USERINFO = {"***:***", "${CAM_USER}:${CAM_PASS}"}


# --- secrets -----------------------------------------------------------------


def read_env_file(path: Path) -> dict[str, str]:
    out: dict[str, str] = {}
    if not path.exists():
        return out
    for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        stripped = line.strip()
        if not stripped or stripped.startswith("#") or "=" not in stripped:
            continue
        key, _, value = stripped.partition("=")
        out[key.strip()] = _parse_dotenv_value(value)
    return out


def read_env() -> dict[str, str]:
    """admin.env (the test login) overlaid by .env (owner-written values)."""
    return {**read_env_file(S / "admin.env"), **read_env_file(S / ".env")}


def squash(text: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"\s+", "", text)


def secret_needles(env: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
    """Whitespace-free search strings per secret kind; values under 6 chars are not searched."""
    user, pw = env.get("CAM_USER", ""), env.get("CAM_PASS", "")
    cam: set[str] = set()
    if pw:
        cam |= {f"{user}:{pw}@", f"{unquote(user)}:{unquote(pw)}@"}
        plain = unquote(pw)
        for value in (pw, plain, html.escape(plain), quote(plain, safe="")):
            if len(value) >= 6:
                cam.add(value)
    out: dict[str, list[str]] = {"camera_password": sorted({squash(c) for c in cam if squash(c)})}
    for kind, key in (("ntfy_topic", "NTFY_TOPIC"), ("ntfy_token", "NTFY_TOKEN")):
        value = squash(env.get(key, ""))
        out[kind] = [value] if len(value) >= 6 else []
    return out


def count_hits(text: str, needles: dict[str, list[str]]) -> dict[str, int]:
    flat = squash(text)
    return {kind: sum(flat.count(n) for n in values) for kind, values in needles.items()}


def unredacted_userinfo(text: str) -> int:
    return sum(1 for m in USERINFO_RE.finditer(text) if m.group(1) not in ALLOWED_USERINFO)


def masker(env: dict[str, str]):
    """Return a function that hides every secret value, URL userinfo and logged passwords."""
    raw_values = [env.get(k, "") for k in ("CAM_PASS", "NTFY_TOPIC", "NTFY_TOKEN")]
    raw_values.append(env.get("WARDEN_ADMIN_PASSWORD", ""))
    pw = env.get("CAM_PASS", "")
    if pw:
        raw_values += [unquote(pw), quote(unquote(pw), safe="")]
    raw_values = sorted({v for v in raw_values if len(v) >= 3}, key=len, reverse=True)
    ntfy = env.get("NTFY_URL", "").rstrip("/")
    endpoint_re = re.compile(re.escape(ntfy) + r"/[^\s?\"'<>]*") if ntfy else None

    def mask(text: str) -> str:
        text = re.sub(r"(rtsps?://)[^\s/@\"'<>]+@", r"\1<userinfo>@", text)
        text = re.sub(
            r"(password\s*[=:]?\s*)(['\"]?)[^\s'\"]+\2", r"\1<redacted>", text, flags=re.I
        )
        if endpoint_re is not None:
            text = endpoint_re.sub("<ntfy-endpoint>", text)
        for value in raw_values:
            text = text.replace(value, "<secret>")
        return text

    return mask


def safe_json(obj: Any, limit: int = 1500) -> str:
    text = masker(read_env())(json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, default=str))
    return text if len(text) <= limit else text[:limit] + "...<cut>"


# --- small helpers -----------------------------------------------------------


def as_utc(value: Any) -> datetime | None:
    """DB datetimes are naive UTC text on SQLite."""
    if value in (None, ""):
        return None
    dt = datetime.fromisoformat(str(value).replace("Z", "+00:00"))
    return dt.replace(tzinfo=UTC) if dt.tzinfo is None else dt.astimezone(UTC)


def local_hms(dt: datetime | None) -> str | None:
    return dt.astimezone().strftime("%H:%M:%S") if dt else None


def db_connect() -> sqlite3.Connection:
    con = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{DB}?mode=ro", uri=True, timeout=10)
    con.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    return con


def short(value: Any) -> Any:
    """Show paths under the scratch folder as <S>/..."""
    return value.replace(str(S), "<S>") if isinstance(value, str) else value


def load_yaml(path: Path) -> dict:
    return yaml.safe_load(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) or {}


def camera_entry(raw: dict) -> dict:
    cams = [c for c in (raw.get("cameras") or []) if isinstance(c, dict)]
    return next((c for c in cams if c.get("name") == CAM), {})


def fetch_status() -> dict:
    with httpx.Client(timeout=5.0) as client:
        resp = client.get(f"{BASE}/status.json")
        resp.raise_for_status()
        return resp.json()


def jpeg_facts(path: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    if not path.is_file():
        return {"exists": False}
    data = path.read_bytes()
    facts: dict[str, Any] = {
        "exists": True,
        "bytes": len(data),
        "jpeg_markers_ok": data[:2] == b"\xff\xd8" and data.rstrip(b"\x00")[-2:] == b"\xff\xd9",
    }
    try:
        import cv2
        import numpy as np

        img = cv2.imdecode(np.frombuffer(data, dtype=np.uint8), cv2.IMREAD_COLOR)
        facts["px"] = None if img is None else [int(img.shape[1]), int(img.shape[0])]
    except Exception as exc:  # cv2 missing or undecodable
        facts["px"] = f"undecodable ({type(exc).__name__})"
    return facts


def under_rec(rel: str | None) -> Path | None:
    if not rel:
        return None
    p = Path(rel)
    return p if p.is_absolute() else REC / p


def proc_cmdlines() -> list[tuple[int, list[bytes]]]:
    me = os.getpid()
    out: list[tuple[int, list[bytes]]] = []
    for entry in Path("/proc").iterdir():
        if not entry.name.isdigit() or int(entry.name) == me:
            continue
        try:
            argv = (entry / "cmdline").read_bytes().split(b"\0")
        except OSError:
            continue
        if argv and argv[0]:
            out.append((int(entry.name), argv))
    return out


def camera_ffmpeg_pids() -> list[int]:
    pids = []
    for pid, argv in proc_cmdlines():
        exe = os.path.basename(argv[0].decode(errors="replace"))
        if exe.startswith(("ffmpeg", "ffprobe")) and any(
            b"videoMain" in a or b"192.168.1.72" in a for a in argv[1:]
        ):
            pids.append(pid)
    return sorted(pids)


def serve_pids() -> list[int]:
    cfg = str(S / "config.yaml").encode()
    pids = []
    for pid, argv in proc_cmdlines():
        exe = os.path.basename(argv[0].decode(errors="replace"))
        if exe == "uv":
            continue
        if b"serve" in argv and cfg in argv and any(a.endswith(b"rtsp-warden") for a in argv):
            pids.append(pid)
    return sorted(pids)


def cpu_ticks(pid: int) -> int | None:
    try:
        fields = Path(f"/proc/{pid}/stat").read_text().rsplit(")", 1)[1].split()
    except OSError:
        return None
    return int(fields[11]) + int(fields[12])  # utime + stime


# --- commands ----------------------------------------------------------------


def cmd_env() -> int:
    env_path = S / ".env"
    print("env_exists:", env_path.exists())
    if not env_path.exists():
        return 1
    print("env_mode:", oct(stat.S_IMODE(env_path.stat().st_mode)))
    env = read_env_file(env_path)
    for key in ENV_KEYS:
        print(f"{key}:", "set" if env.get(key) else ("empty" if key in env else "missing"))
    user, pw = env.get("CAM_USER", ""), env.get("CAM_PASS", "")
    url = CAM_URL_REF.replace("${CAM_USER}", user).replace("${CAM_PASS}", pw)
    try:
        parts = urlsplit(url)
        parsed = (parts.hostname, parts.port, parts.path)
        print("camera_url_parses:", parsed == ("192.168.1.72", 554, "/videoMain"))
        same = unquote(parts.username or "") == unquote(user) and unquote(
            parts.password or ""
        ) == unquote(pw)
        print("camera_userinfo_roundtrip:", same)
    except ValueError as exc:
        print("camera_url_parses: False", type(exc).__name__)
    print("bad_percent_escape:", re.search(r"%(?![0-9A-Fa-f]{2})", user + pw) is not None)
    print("raw_reserved_chars_in_credentials:", any(c in user + pw for c in "@/?# "))
    nurl = env.get("NTFY_URL", "")
    print("ntfy_url_scheme:", urlsplit(nurl).scheme if nurl else None)
    print("ntfy_url_has_path:", bool(urlsplit(nurl).path.strip("/")) if nurl else None)
    print("ntfy_topic_length:", len(env.get("NTFY_TOPIC", "")))
    return 0


def cmd_config() -> int:
    env = read_env()
    text = (S / "config.yaml").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    raw = yaml.safe_load(text) or {}
    cams = [c.get("name") for c in (raw.get("cameras") or []) if isinstance(c, dict)]
    print("camera_names:", cams)
    cam = camera_entry(raw)
    print("main_url_is_env_ref:", cam.get("main_url") == CAM_URL_REF)
    print("sub_url_key_present:", "sub_url" in cam)
    for key in ("detect_fps", "track_grace_seconds", "min_track_frames", "detect_classes"):
        print(f"{key}:", cam.get(key))
    rec = cam.get("record") or {}
    print(
        "record:",
        {
            "enabled": rec.get("enabled"),
            "output_dir": short(rec.get("output_dir")),
            "main_chunk_seconds": (rec.get("main") or {}).get("chunk_seconds"),
        },
    )
    proxy = cam.get("proxy") or {}
    print("proxy:", {k: proxy.get(k) for k in ("enabled", "mode", "stream", "port", "bind_host")})
    for i, spec in enumerate(cam.get("detectors") or []):
        keys = ("type", "model", "device", "fps", "interval_seconds", "min_confidence", "enabled")
        print(f"detectors[{i}]:", {k: spec.get(k) for k in keys if k in spec})
    for rule in cam.get("rules") or []:
        keys = ("name", "labels", "zones", "min_confidence", "between", "cooldown_seconds", "clip")
        print("rule:", {**{k: rule.get(k) for k in keys}, "actions": rule.get("actions")})
    for action in raw.get("actions") or []:
        refs = {k: action.get(k) == "${NTFY_" + k.upper() + "}" for k in ("url", "topic", "token")}
        print("action:", {"name": action.get("name"), "type": action.get("type"), "env_refs": refs})
    rt = raw.get("runtime") or {}
    keys = ("models_dir", "workspace_dir", "ffmpeg_loglevel")
    print("runtime:", {k: short(rt.get(k)) for k in keys})
    print("clips:", raw.get("clips"))
    print("config_secret_hits:", count_hits(text, secret_needles(env)))
    print("config_unredacted_userinfo:", unredacted_userinfo(text))
    return 0


def alembic_config():
    from alembic.config import Config

    cfg = Config()
    cfg.set_main_option("script_location", SCRIPT_LOCATION)
    cfg.set_main_option("sqlalchemy.url", f"sqlite:///{DB}")
    return cfg


def cmd_seed_0002() -> int:
    if DB.exists():
        print("seed: refused, warden.db already exists")
        return 1
    os.environ["WARDEN_DB_URL"] = f"sqlite:///{DB}"
    from alembic import command

    command.upgrade(alembic_config(), "0002_clips")
    con = sqlite3.connect(DB)
    meta = json.dumps({"stream": "main", "ts_unix": 1790856000.0})
    con.execute(
        "INSERT INTO events (camera_id, event_type, severity, message, metadata_json, created_at)"
        " VALUES (NULL, 'motion', 'info', ?, ?, '2026-10-01 12:00:00')",
        ("motion detected on foscam-c1/main (confidence=0.80)", meta),
    )
    con.commit()
    rev = con.execute("SELECT version_num FROM alembic_version").fetchone()[0]
    count = con.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM events").fetchone()[0]
    con.close()
    print("seed: revision", rev, "events", count)
    return 0


def cmd_db() -> int:
    from alembic.script import ScriptDirectory

    try:
        head = ScriptDirectory.from_config(alembic_config()).get_current_head()
    except Exception as exc:  # script location missing or broken
        head = f"unknown ({type(exc).__name__})"
    print("db_exists:", DB.exists())
    if not DB.exists():
        return 1
    con = db_connect()
    tables = sorted(
        r[0]
        for r in con.execute(
            "SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name NOT LIKE 'sqlite_%'"
        )
    )
    rev = [r[0] for r in con.execute("SELECT version_num FROM alembic_version")]
    print("revision:", rev, "head:", head, "at_head:", rev == [head])
    print("tables:", tables)
    print("backups:", sorted(p.name for p in S.glob("warden.db.bak-*")))
    cols = [r[1] for r in con.execute("PRAGMA table_info(events)")]
    print("events_columns:", cols)
    row = con.execute("SELECT * FROM events WHERE id = 1").fetchone()
    if row is not None:
        keys = ("event_type", "camera_name", "label", "message")
        print("legacy_row:", {k: row[k] for k in keys if k in row.keys()})
    print("events:", con.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM events").fetchone()[0])
    if "action_runs" in tables:
        print("action_runs:", con.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM action_runs").fetchone()[0])
    return 0


def cmd_model(name: str) -> int:
    import hashlib

    from rtsp_warden.detectors.model_registry import load_descriptor, model_file_path

    desc = load_descriptor(name, MODELS)
    path = model_file_path(desc, MODELS)
    source = "user" if desc.base_dir.resolve().is_relative_to(MODELS.resolve()) else "built-in"
    print("model:", desc.name, "descriptor:", source)
    print("file:", path.relative_to(S) if path.is_relative_to(S) else path)
    print("exists:", path.is_file())
    print(
        "part_files:",
        sorted(p.name for p in path.parent.glob("*.part")) if path.parent.is_dir() else [],
    )
    print("pinned_sha256:", desc.sha256)
    if path.is_file():
        digest = hashlib.sha256()
        with path.open("rb") as fh:
            for chunk in iter(lambda: fh.read(1 << 20), b""):
                digest.update(chunk)
        print("bytes:", path.stat().st_size)
        print("sha256:", digest.hexdigest())
        print("sha256_matches_pin:", digest.hexdigest() == desc.sha256)
    return 0


def summarize(data: dict) -> dict[str, Any]:
    now = float(data.get("now") or time.time())
    cam = next((c for c in data.get("cameras", []) if c.get("name") == CAM), None)
    if cam is None:
        return {"present": False, "cameras": len(data.get("cameras", []))}
    main = (cam.get("streams") or {}).get("main") or {}
    ingest = main.get("ingest") or {}

    def age(key: str) -> float | None:
        value = main.get(key)
        return None if value is None else round(now - float(value), 1)

    url = str(main.get("source_url", ""))
    return {
        "present": True,
        "ok": cam.get("ok"),
        "streams": sorted(cam.get("streams") or {}),
        "main_running": ingest.get("running"),
        "ingest_pid": ingest.get("pid"),
        "record_enabled": main.get("record_enabled"),
        "frame_age_s": age("last_frame_at"),
        "segment_age_s": age("last_segment_at"),
        "source_url_redacted": "@" not in url or "***" in url,
        "has_detection_key": "detection" in cam,
    }


def print_detection(data: dict) -> None:
    cam = next((c for c in data.get("cameras", []) if c.get("name") == CAM), {})
    det = cam.get("detection")
    print("detection:", safe_json(det) if det is not None else "missing")
    found: list[str] = []

    def walk(obj: Any) -> None:
        if isinstance(obj, dict):
            for k, v in obj.items():
                if k in ("provider", "fallback_warning", "error") and v:
                    found.append(f"{k}={v}")
                walk(v)
        elif isinstance(obj, list):
            for v in obj:
                walk(v)

    walk(cam)
    print("provider_error_fields:", masker(read_env())("; ".join(found)) or "none")


def cmd_status() -> int:
    data = fetch_status()
    print("status:", summarize(data))
    print_detection(data)
    return 0


def cmd_status_file(path: Path) -> int:
    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    try:
        data = json.loads(text)
    except ValueError:
        print(f"status-file: not valid JSON ({len(text)} bytes)")
        return 1
    print("cameras:", [c.get("name") for c in data.get("cameras", [])])
    print_detection(data)
    return 0


def output_segment(argv: list[str], index: int) -> list[str]:
    start = max((j for j in range(index) if argv[j] == "-map"), default=0)
    return argv[start:index]


def option(seg: list[str], flag: str) -> str | None:
    return seg[seg.index(flag) + 1] if flag in seg and seg.index(flag) + 1 < len(seg) else None


def cmd_tap() -> int:
    data = fetch_status()
    cam = next((c for c in data.get("cameras", []) if c.get("name") == CAM), {})
    ingest = (((cam.get("streams") or {}).get("main") or {}).get("ingest")) or {}
    argv = [str(a) for a in ingest.get("argv") or []]
    pid = ingest.get("pid")
    outs = [(i, a) for i, a in enumerate(argv) if a.startswith("pipe:") and a != "pipe:1"]
    print("ingest_pid:", pid)
    if "pipe:1" in argv:
        seg = output_segment(argv, argv.index("pipe:1"))
        print("proxy_mjpeg:", {"rate": option(seg, "-r"), "filter": option(seg, "-vf")})
    if not outs:
        print("tap_output: none")
        return 1
    index, target = outs[-1]
    seg = output_segment(argv, index)
    print("tap_output:", target, "tap_outputs_total:", len(outs))
    print("tap_rate:", option(seg, "-r"))
    print("tap_filter:", option(seg, "-vf"))
    try:
        link = os.readlink(f"/proc/{pid}/fd/{int(target.split(':', 1)[1])}")
        print("tap_fd_is_pipe:", link.startswith("pipe:"))
    except (OSError, ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
        print("tap_fd_is_pipe: False", type(exc).__name__)
    return 0


def cmd_wait(state: str, timeout_s: float) -> int:
    if state not in ("running", "stopped"):
        raise SystemExit("STATE must be running or stopped")
    start = time.monotonic()
    last: dict[str, Any] = {}
    done = False
    while True:
        try:
            last = summarize(fetch_status())
            age = last.get("frame_age_s")
            done = (
                state == "running"
                and last.get("main_running") is True
                and age is not None
                and age < 5.0
            )
        except (httpx.HTTPError, OSError) as exc:
            last = {"error": type(exc).__name__}
            done = state == "stopped"
        if done or time.monotonic() - start >= timeout_s:
            break
        time.sleep(1.0)
    print(
        f"wait {state}: {'reached' if done else 'TIMEOUT'} after {time.monotonic() - start:.1f} s"
    )
    print("status:", last)
    return 0 if done else 1


def cmd_wait_log(log: str, text: str, timeout_s: float, min_count: int) -> int:
    path = S / log
    mask = masker(read_env())
    start = time.monotonic()
    lines: list[str] = []
    while True:
        if path.exists():
            content = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
            lines = [ln for ln in content.splitlines() if text in ln]
        if len(lines) >= min_count or time.monotonic() - start >= timeout_s:
            break
        time.sleep(1.0)
    verdict = "found" if len(lines) >= min_count else "TIMEOUT"
    print(f"wait-log {text!r}: {verdict} after {time.monotonic() - start:.1f} s")
    print("count:", len(lines))
    for ln in lines[-3:]:
        print("  ", mask(ln.rstrip())[:400])
    return 0 if len(lines) >= min_count else 1


def cmd_log_tail(log: str, n: int) -> int:
    path = S / log
    mask = masker(read_env())
    for ln in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines()[-n:]:
        print(mask(ln.rstrip())[:400])
    return 0


def seg_facts() -> dict[str, Any]:
    d = REC / CAM / "main"
    files = sorted(d.glob("*.ts"), key=lambda p: p.stat().st_mtime) if d.is_dir() else []
    newest = files[-1] if files else None
    return {
        "count": len(files),
        "total_bytes": sum(p.stat().st_size for p in files),
        "newest_age_s": round(time.time() - newest.stat().st_mtime, 1) if newest else None,
    }


def cmd_segments(seconds: float) -> int:
    before = seg_facts()
    time.sleep(seconds)
    after = seg_facts()
    print("before:", before)
    print("after: ", after)
    grew = after["total_bytes"] > before["total_bytes"] or after["count"] > before["count"]
    print(f"grew_in_{seconds:g}s:", grew)
    return 0


def cmd_procs() -> int:
    print("camera_ffmpeg_processes:", len(camera_ffmpeg_pids()), "pids:", camera_ffmpeg_pids())
    print("serve_processes:", len(serve_pids()), "pids:", serve_pids())
    return 0


def cmd_stop(timeout_s: float) -> int:
    pids = serve_pids()
    for pid in pids:
        os.kill(pid, signal.SIGINT)
    start = time.monotonic()
    while serve_pids() and time.monotonic() - start < timeout_s:
        time.sleep(0.5)
    left = serve_pids()
    print("signalled:", pids, "stopped:", not left, f"after {time.monotonic() - start:.1f} s")
    print("camera_ffmpeg_processes:", len(camera_ffmpeg_pids()))
    return 0 if not left else 1


def cmd_cpu(seconds: float) -> int:
    hz = os.sysconf("SC_CLK_TCK")
    groups = {"serve": serve_pids(), "camera_ffmpeg": camera_ffmpeg_pids()}
    before = {k: [cpu_ticks(p) for p in v] for k, v in groups.items()}
    time.sleep(seconds)
    for name, pids in groups.items():
        after = [cpu_ticks(p) for p in pids]
        used = sum(
            a - b
            for a, b in zip(after, before[name], strict=True)
            if a is not None and b is not None
        )
        print(
            f"{name}_cpu_percent_of_one_core:", round(100.0 * used / hz / seconds, 1), "pids:", pids
        )
    for pid in groups["serve"]:
        for line in Path(f"/proc/{pid}/status").read_text().splitlines():
            if line.startswith("VmRSS:"):
                print("serve_rss_mib:", round(int(line.split()[1]) / 1024, 1))
    return 0


def cmd_gpu() -> int:
    exe = shutil.which("nvidia-smi")
    if exe is None:
        print("nvidia_smi: missing")
        return 1
    out = subprocess.run(
        [exe, "--query-compute-apps=pid,used_memory", "--format=csv,noheader,nounits"],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        timeout=20,
    ).stdout
    apps = {}
    for line in out.splitlines():
        parts = [p.strip() for p in line.split(",")]
        if len(parts) == 2 and parts[0].isdigit():
            apps[int(parts[0])] = parts[1]
    pids = serve_pids()
    on_gpu = [p for p in pids if p in apps]
    print("serve_pids:", pids, "serve_on_gpu:", bool(on_gpu))
    print("serve_gpu_mib:", [apps[p] for p in on_gpu])
    return 0


def load_events(after_id: int) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    con = db_connect()
    rows = [
        dict(r) for r in con.execute("SELECT * FROM events WHERE id > ? ORDER BY id", (after_id,))
    ]
    for row in rows:
        row["runs"] = [
            dict(r)
            for r in con.execute(
                "SELECT action_name, status, error FROM action_runs WHERE event_id = ? ORDER BY id",
                (row["id"],),
            )
        ]
        try:
            row["meta"] = json.loads(row.get("metadata_json") or "{}")
        except ValueError:
            row["meta"] = {}
    con.close()
    return rows


def kind_of(row: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    if row.get("event_type") == "test":
        return "test"
    if row.get("event_type") == "motion" or row.get("label") == "motion":
        return "motion"
    return "object"


def marks() -> dict[str, Any]:
    path = S / "marks.json"
    return json.loads(path.read_text()) if path.exists() else {}


def cmd_mark(name: str) -> int:
    con = db_connect()
    max_id = con.execute("SELECT coalesce(max(id), 0) FROM events").fetchone()[0]
    con.close()
    data = marks()
    data[name] = {"t": time.time(), "max_event_id": int(max_id)}
    (S / "marks.json").write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=2))
    print(f"mark {name}: newest event id {max_id} at {datetime.now().strftime('%H:%M:%S')}")
    return 0


def cmd_cooldown_wait(seconds: float) -> int:
    fired = [
        e
        for e in load_events(0)
        if kind_of(e) == "object"
        and e.get("label") == "person"
        and any(r["status"] == "ok" for r in e["runs"])
    ]
    if not fired:
        print("cooldown-wait: no notified person event yet; no wait")
        return 0
    opened = as_utc(fired[-1]["created_at"])
    assert opened is not None
    remaining = opened.timestamp() + seconds - time.time()
    wait_s = max(0.0, remaining)
    print(f"cooldown-wait: event {fired[-1]['id']} opened {local_hms(opened)}; wait {wait_s:.0f} s")
    if remaining > 0:
        time.sleep(remaining)
    return 0


def settled(rows: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> bool:
    """At least one event; every event has ended; each object or test event has an
    action run, a suppressed_by note, or ended at least 10 s ago (no rule matched)."""
    if not rows:
        return False
    for e in rows:
        ended = as_utc(e.get("ended_at"))
        if ended is None:
            return False
        waiting = not e["runs"] and not e["meta"].get("suppressed_by")
        if kind_of(e) != "motion" and waiting and time.time() - ended.timestamp() < 10.0:
            return False
    return True


def describe(e: dict[str, Any], mark_t: float | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    created, ended = as_utc(e.get("created_at")), as_utc(e.get("ended_at"))
    mask = masker(read_env())
    return {
        "id": e["id"],
        "kind": kind_of(e),
        "event_type": e.get("event_type"),
        "label": e.get("label"),
        "confidence": None if e.get("confidence") is None else round(float(e["confidence"]), 2),
        "zone": e.get("zone"),
        "track_id": e.get("track_id"),
        "opened": local_hms(created),
        "opened_after_mark_s": round(created.timestamp() - mark_t, 1)
        if created and mark_t
        else None,
        "ended": local_hms(ended),
        "duration_s": round((ended - created).total_seconds(), 1) if created and ended else None,
        "thumbnail": e.get("thumbnail_path"),
        "thumbnail_file": jpeg_facts(under_rec(e.get("thumbnail_path")))
        if e.get("thumbnail_path")
        else None,
        "clip": e.get("clip_path"),
        "runs": [{**r, "error": mask(r["error"]) if r.get("error") else None} for r in e["runs"]],
        "suppressed_by": e["meta"].get("suppressed_by"),
        "meta_keys": sorted(e["meta"]),
    }


def cmd_visit(name: str, timeout_s: float) -> int:
    mark = marks().get(name)
    if mark is None:
        raise SystemExit(f"no mark named {name!r}; run: mark {name}")
    start = time.monotonic()
    rows = load_events(mark["max_event_id"])
    while not settled(rows) and time.monotonic() - start < timeout_s:
        time.sleep(2.0)
        rows = load_events(mark["max_event_id"])
    verdict = "settled" if settled(rows) else "TIMEOUT"
    print(f"visit {name}: {verdict} after {time.monotonic() - start:.1f} s")
    for e in rows:
        print("event:", describe(e, mark["t"]))
    person = [e for e in rows if kind_of(e) == "object" and e.get("label") == "person"]
    print(
        "summary:",
        {
            "person_events": len(person),
            "other_object_events": len(
                [e for e in rows if kind_of(e) == "object" and e.get("label") != "person"]
            ),
            "motion_events": len([e for e in rows if kind_of(e) == "motion"]),
            "test_events": len([e for e in rows if kind_of(e) == "test"]),
            "runs_ok": sum(r["status"] == "ok" for e in rows for r in e["runs"]),
            "runs_failed": sum(r["status"] != "ok" for e in rows for r in e["runs"]),
            "suppressed": sum(bool(e["meta"].get("suppressed_by")) for e in rows),
        },
    )
    return 0 if settled(rows) else 1


def cmd_clip(event_id: int, timeout_s: float) -> int:
    start = time.monotonic()
    row = None
    while time.monotonic() - start < timeout_s:
        con = db_connect()
        row = con.execute("SELECT * FROM events WHERE id = ?", (event_id,)).fetchone()
        con.close()
        if row is not None and row["clip_path"]:
            break
        time.sleep(2.0)
    if row is None or not row["clip_path"]:
        print(
            f"clip {event_id}: TIMEOUT after {time.monotonic() - start:.1f} s (clip_path not set)"
        )
        return 1
    path = under_rec(row["clip_path"])
    assert path is not None
    print(f"clip {event_id}: set after {time.monotonic() - start:.1f} s")
    print("clip_path:", row["clip_path"], "ext:", path.suffix, "exists:", path.is_file())
    raw = load_yaml(S / "config.yaml").get("clips") or {}
    pre, post = float(raw.get("pre_seconds", 10.0)), float(raw.get("post_seconds", 10.0))
    cap = float(raw.get("max_duration", 120.0))
    created, ended = as_utc(row["created_at"]), as_utc(row["ended_at"])
    window = min(pre + (ended - created).total_seconds() + post, cap) if created and ended else None
    probe = subprocess.run(
        [
            "ffprobe",
            "-v",
            "error",
            "-show_entries",
            "format=format_name,duration:stream=codec_type,codec_name,width,height",
            "-of",
            "json",
            str(path),
        ],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        timeout=60,
    )
    if probe.returncode != 0:
        print("ffprobe_rc:", probe.returncode, masker(read_env())(probe.stderr.strip())[:300])
        return 1
    info = json.loads(probe.stdout)
    video = next((s for s in info.get("streams", []) if s.get("codec_type") == "video"), {})
    duration = float(info.get("format", {}).get("duration") or 0.0)
    print("bytes:", path.stat().st_size, "format:", info.get("format", {}).get("format_name"))
    print("video:", video.get("codec_name"), f"{video.get('width')}x{video.get('height')}")
    print(
        "duration_s:",
        round(duration, 2),
        "window_s:",
        None if window is None else round(window, 2),
        "delta_s:",
        None if window is None else round(duration - window, 2),
    )
    return 0


def report(name: str, text: str, needles: dict[str, list[str]]) -> bool:
    hits = count_hits(text, needles)
    raw = unredacted_userinfo(text)
    print(
        f"{name}: " + " ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in hits.items()) + f" unredacted_userinfo={raw}"
    )
    return not any(hits.values()) and raw == 0


def cmd_leaks() -> int:
    env = read_env()
    needles = secret_needles(env)
    for kind, values in needles.items():
        if not values:
            print(f"note: {kind} is not searched (unset or shorter than 6 characters)")
    clean = True
    for log in sorted(S.glob("serve-*.log")) + sorted(S.glob("status-cli-*")):
        clean &= report(log.name, log.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"), needles)
    clean &= report("config.yaml", (S / "config.yaml").read_text(encoding="utf-8"), needles)
    event_ids: list[int] = []
    if DB.exists():
        con = db_connect()
        tables = {
            r[0]
            for r in con.execute(
                "SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name NOT LIKE 'sqlite_%'"
            )
        }
        chunks = [
            " ".join(str(v) for v in r)
            for r in con.execute("SELECT message, metadata_json FROM events")
        ]
        if "action_runs" in tables:
            chunks += [
                str(r[0])
                for r in con.execute("SELECT error FROM action_runs WHERE error IS NOT NULL")
            ]
        event_ids = [r[0] for r in con.execute("SELECT id FROM events ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 20")]
        con.close()
        clean &= report("db events/action_runs text", "\n".join(chunks), needles)
    with httpx.Client(base_url=BASE, timeout=15.0, follow_redirects=False) as client:
        try:
            client.get("/login", headers={"Accept": "text/html"})
        except httpx.HTTPError as exc:
            print(f"server not reachable ({type(exc).__name__}); pages skipped")
            print("LEAK CHECK:", "PASS (files only)" if clean else "FAIL")
            return 0 if clean else 1
        resp = client.post(
            "/login",
            data={
                "username": env.get("WARDEN_ADMIN_USERNAME", "admin"),
                "password": env.get("WARDEN_ADMIN_PASSWORD", ""),
                "csrf_token": client.cookies.get("warden_csrf") or "",
                "next": "/",
            },
        )
        logged_in = resp.status_code == 303 and client.cookies.get("warden_session") is not None
        print("login:", "ok" if logged_in else f"FAILED (status {resp.status_code})")
        for path in PAGES + tuple(f"/events/{i}" for i in event_ids):
            page = client.get(path, headers={"Accept": "text/html"})
            clean &= report(f"GET {path} [{page.status_code}]", page.text, needles)
    print("LEAK CHECK:", "PASS" if clean else "FAIL")
    return 0 if clean else 1


def cmd_scan(path: Path) -> int:
    ok = report(
        str(path.name),
        path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"),
        secret_needles(read_env()),
    )
    print("SCAN:", "PASS" if ok else "FAIL")
    return 0 if ok else 1


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    if not argv:
        print(__doc__)
        return 2
    cmd, rest = argv[0], argv[1:]

    def arg(i: int, default: str) -> str:
        return rest[i] if len(rest) > i else default

    table = {
        "env": lambda: cmd_env(),
        "config": lambda: cmd_config(),
        "seed-0002": lambda: cmd_seed_0002(),
        "db": lambda: cmd_db(),
        "model": lambda: cmd_model(arg(0, "yolox-s")),
        "status": lambda: cmd_status(),
        "status-file": lambda: cmd_status_file(Path(rest[0])),
        "tap": lambda: cmd_tap(),
        "wait": lambda: cmd_wait(rest[0], float(arg(1, "45"))),
        "wait-log": lambda: cmd_wait_log(rest[0], rest[1], float(arg(2, "60")), int(arg(3, "1"))),
        "log-tail": lambda: cmd_log_tail(rest[0], int(arg(1, "40"))),
        "segments": lambda: cmd_segments(float(arg(0, "20"))),
        "procs": lambda: cmd_procs(),
        "stop": lambda: cmd_stop(float(arg(0, "30"))),
        "cpu": lambda: cmd_cpu(float(arg(0, "20"))),
        "gpu": lambda: cmd_gpu(),
        "mark": lambda: cmd_mark(rest[0]),
        "cooldown-wait": lambda: cmd_cooldown_wait(float(rest[0])),
        "visit": lambda: cmd_visit(rest[0], float(arg(1, "90"))),
        "clip": lambda: cmd_clip(int(rest[0]), float(arg(1, "120"))),
        "leaks": lambda: cmd_leaks(),
        "scan": lambda: cmd_scan(Path(rest[0])),
    }
    if cmd not in table:
        print(__doc__)
        return 2
    return table[cmd]()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))
```
